Why preach, why prepare, and how to choose a text — the seven gateways into a Biblical sermon.
Kwa nini tuhubiri, kwa nini tujiandae, na jinsi ya kuchagua kifungu — milango saba ya kuingia katika mahubiri ya Kibiblia.
1.1 Why Lay and Bivocational Preaching Matters
1.1 Kwa Nini Mahubiri ya Walei na ya Wachungaji Wenye Kazi Mbili ni Muhimu

Forty percent of people surveyed list fear of public speaking as their greatest dread. We are more afraid of speaking in public than we are of dying. So when God calls a layperson, a Sunday-school teacher, or a bivocational pastor to preach, the response is often Moses' response: "Who am I that I should go?" The fear is real, the sense of inadequacy is honest, and the obstacle of inadequate training is genuine. And yet the call comes anyway, because the church across every generation has needed more preachers than the seminary system can produce. WiseSpeak exists to equip those whom God has called but the system has not reached.

Asilimia arobaini ya watu waliohojiwa wanataja hofu ya kuzungumza hadharani kuwa ndilo jambo wanaloliogopa kuliko yote. Tunaogopa kuzungumza mbele ya watu kuliko tunavyoogopa kufa. Kwa hiyo Mungu anapomwita mlei, mwalimu wa Shule ya Jumapili, au mchungaji mwenye kazi mbili (anayefanya kazi nyingine ya kujipatia riziki) ahubiri, mara nyingi jibu lake ni lile la Musa: "Mimi ni nani, hata niende?" Hofu hiyo ni ya kweli, hisia ya kutotosha ni ya dhati, na kizuizi cha kukosa mafunzo ya kutosha ni halisi. Hata hivyo wito unakuja, kwa sababu kanisa katika kila kizazi limehitaji wahubiri wengi kuliko mfumo wa vyuo vya theolojia unavyoweza kuwatoa. WiseSpeak ipo ili kuwaandaa wale ambao Mungu amewaita lakini mfumo huo haujawafikia.

There are four reasons the layperson should accept the call to preach. The first is Biblical. Amos was not a professional. He told the king of Israel plainly, "I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet's son" (Amos 7:14). He kept livestock and tended sycamore trees. God called him out of that ordinary life to speak prophetic words to a nation. Moses had been raised in Pharaoh's court but spent forty years as a shepherd before God appeared in the burning bush. When Moses protested that he was not eloquent, the Lord answered, "Who hath made man's mouth?" (Exodus 4:11). Jesus came into the world as a proclaimer; someone has said that God had only one Son and made Him a preacher. Paul earned his living by making tents and yet planted churches across the Roman world. Philip is the only person in Scripture explicitly called an evangelist (Acts 21:8), and he was a deacon by office; even his daughters preached. The early Christian movement was overwhelmingly a lay movement. Most of its preachers earned their living at a trade and proclaimed the gospel as the second labor of their lives.

Kuna sababu nne kwa nini mlei anapaswa kuukubali wito wa kuhubiri. Ya kwanza ni ya Kibiblia. Amosi hakuwa mtaalamu wa kazi hiyo. Alimwambia mfalme wa Israeli waziwazi, "Mimi sikuwa nabii, wala sikuwa mwana wa nabii" (Amosi 7:14). Alikuwa mfugaji wa mifugo na mtunzaji wa mikuyu. Mungu alimwita kutoka katika maisha hayo ya kawaida ili anene maneno ya kinabii kwa taifa zima. Musa alikuwa amelelewa katika jumba la Farao, lakini alikaa miaka arobaini akiwa mchungaji wa kondoo kabla Mungu hajamtokea katika kichaka kilichokuwa kikiwaka moto. Musa alipolalamika kwamba yeye si mtu mwenye ufasaha wa kusema, BWANA alimjibu, "Ni nani aliyeumba kinywa cha mwanadamu?" (Kutoka 4:11). Yesu alikuja ulimwenguni kama mtangazaji; mtu mmoja amesema kwamba Mungu alikuwa na Mwana mmoja tu, naye akamfanya kuwa mhubiri. Paulo alijipatia riziki kwa kushona mahema, na bado alipanda makanisa katika ulimwengu wote wa Kirumi. Filipo ndiye mtu pekee katika Maandiko anayeitwa waziwazi mwinjilisti (Matendo 21:8), naye kwa cheo alikuwa shemasi; hata binti zake walihubiri. Vuguvugu la Kikristo la mwanzo kwa kiasi kikubwa lilikuwa vuguvugu la walei. Wengi wa wahubiri wake walijipatia riziki kwa kazi za mikono na kuitangaza Injili kama kazi ya pili ya maisha yao.

The second reason is historical. The Methodist revival in England rested heavily on lay preachers whose names are now forgotten. The Baptists, Congregationalists, and Brethren used them too. North America in its frontier years had few ordained ministers; one of the farmers who plowed his field six days a week would stand up and preach on Sunday. Dwight L. Moody chose to remain a layman though he served full-time in ministry. The work of God advanced because lay people stood up to speak when no professional was available.

Sababu ya pili ni ya kihistoria. Uamsho wa Kimethodisti huko Uingereza ulitegemea sana wahubiri walei ambao majina yao sasa yamesahauliwa. Wabaptisti, Wakongregationalisti, na Ndugu (Brethren) nao waliwatumia. Amerika ya Kaskazini katika miaka yake ya mipakani (ya walowezi wa mwanzo) ilikuwa na wachungaji wachache waliowekwa wakfu; mmoja wa wakulima waliolima shamba lake siku sita kwa juma alisimama na kuhubiri siku ya Jumapili. Dwight L. Moody alichagua kubaki mlei ingawa alihudumu katika huduma muda wote. Kazi ya Mungu ilisonga mbele kwa sababu walei walisimama kunena wakati hakukuwa na mtaalamu yeyote.

The third reason is the priesthood of all believers. In the Old Testament the priesthood was a closed office held by descendants of Aaron. In the New Testament, Peter declares of the whole church: "Ye also, as living stones, are built up a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood" (1 Peter 2:5). This means that we do not merely have a priesthood — we are a priesthood. The believer's task is to exercise his gifts for the glory of God, and if the gift of speech is among them, the Lord will use that gift in building His church.

Sababu ya tatu ni ukuhani wa waumini wote. Katika Agano la Kale ukuhani ulikuwa cheo kilichofungwa, kilichoshikwa na wazao wa Haruni. Katika Agano Jipya, Petro anatangaza juu ya kanisa zima: "Ninyi nanyi, kama mawe yaliyo hai, mnajengwa mwe nyumba ya roho, ukuhani mtakatifu" (1 Petro 2:5). Hii ina maana kwamba hatuna tu ukuhani — sisi tu ukuhani. Kazi ya mwamini ni kutumia karama zake kwa utukufu wa Mungu, na ikiwa karama ya kunena ni mojawapo, Bwana ataitumia karama hiyo katika kulijenga kanisa lake.

The fourth reason is simply that lay preachers can be effective. There are not enough ordained clergy to meet every preaching need today, and there never have been. The Gideons have preached for generations and have done a fine job. Pastors regularly leave their pulpits in the hands of capable lay speakers when they must be away. The work continues because God uses what is offered to Him.

Sababu ya nne ni kwamba tu wahubiri walei wanaweza kuwa na matokeo mazuri. Hakuna wachungaji wa kutosha waliowekwa wakfu kukidhi kila hitaji la kuhubiri leo, na haijawahi kuwepo. Wagideoni (The Gideons) wamehubiri kwa vizazi vingi na wamefanya kazi nzuri. Mara kwa mara wachungaji huacha mimbari zao mikononi mwa wanenaji walei wenye uwezo wanapolazimika kuwa mbali. Kazi inaendelea kwa sababu Mungu hutumia kile kinachotolewa kwake.
1.2 Why Prepare to Preach
1.2 Kwa Nini Tujiandae Kuhubiri

There are groups in the church that advocate preaching without preparation. They believe the preacher need only stand up and rely on the Holy Spirit for inspiration. The lay people who later comment on this kind of preaching almost always describe the same experience: the sermons are long, disorganized, and repeat the same ideas over and over. Five reasons stand against unprepared preaching.

Kuna makundi ndani ya kanisa yanayotetea kuhubiri bila maandalizi. Wanaamini kwamba mhubiri anahitaji tu kusimama na kumtegemea Roho Mtakatifu kwa uvuvio. Walei ambao baadaye hutoa maoni juu ya mahubiri ya aina hii karibu kila mara hueleza uzoefu ule ule: mahubiri ni marefu, hayana mpangilio, na yanarudia mawazo yale yale tena na tena. Sababu tano zinapinga kuhubiri bila maandalizi.

First, God demands it. Paul charged young Timothy: "Give diligence to present thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, handling aright the word of truth" (2 Timothy 2:15). It is an awesome thing to speak for God. We are not prophets in the strict sense; we do not receive direct revelation. We are not apostles; we have not seen the risen Christ with physical eyes. We are stewards of the Bible, and our authority is derivative — it depends entirely upon how faithfully we have studied the text. G. Campbell Morgan closeted himself with his Bible every morning and would let nothing but a genuine emergency interrupt him.

Kwanza, Mungu anayadai. Paulo alimwagiza kijana Timotheo: "Jitahidi kujionyesha kuwa umekubaliwa na Mungu, mtenda kazi asiye na sababu ya kutahayari, ukitumia kwa halali neno la kweli" (2 Timotheo 2:15). Ni jambo zito na la kutisha kunena kwa niaba ya Mungu. Sisi si manabii kwa maana halisi ya neno hilo; hatupokei ufunuo wa moja kwa moja. Sisi si mitume; hatujamwona Kristo aliyefufuka kwa macho ya kimwili. Sisi ni mawakili wa Biblia, na mamlaka yetu ni ya kutokana na mamlaka mengine — yanategemea kabisa jinsi tulivyokisoma kifungu kwa uaminifu. G. Campbell Morgan alijifungia pamoja na Biblia yake kila asubuhi, wala hakuruhusu kitu chochote kumkatiza isipokuwa dharura ya kweli.

Second, the task itself demands it. Every Sunday millions gather to hear a word from God. In Jeremiah's day, false prophets told King Zedekiah whatever he wanted to hear, while the true prophet sat in prison. When the national crisis came, the king sent for Jeremiah in secret and asked, "Is there any word from the Lord?" That is the question every congregation, in every generation, brings to church on Sunday morning. The preacher has no right to give them anything else.

Pili, kazi yenyewe inayadai. Kila Jumapili mamilioni hukusanyika kusikia neno kutoka kwa Mungu. Katika siku za Yeremia, manabii wa uongo walimwambia Mfalme Sedekia lolote alilotaka kusikia, wakati nabii wa kweli alikuwa amekaa gerezani. Shida ya kitaifa ilipofika, mfalme alimwita Yeremia kwa siri akauliza, "Je! Kuna neno lo lote litokalo kwa BWANA?" Hilo ndilo swali ambalo kila kusanyiko, katika kila kizazi, huleta kanisani Jumapili asubuhi. Mhubiri hana haki ya kuwapa kitu kingine chochote.

Third, preparation removes the fear of uncertainty. Much of the dread of speaking comes from the inner whisper, "I have nothing to say." Preparation answers that whisper. The preacher who has studied does not need to wonder whether the next sentence will arrive; he has placed his sentences in order ahead of time. The fear does not disappear entirely, but it becomes manageable.

Tatu, maandalizi huondoa hofu ya kutokuwa na uhakika. Sehemu kubwa ya woga wa kunena hutokana na mnong'ono wa ndani unaosema, "Sina la kusema." Maandalizi hujibu mnong'ono huo. Mhubiri aliyejifunza hahitaji kujiuliza kama sentensi inayofuata itakuja; ameshazipanga sentensi zake kwa utaratibu kabla ya wakati. Hofu haitoweki kabisa, lakini inakuwa kitu kinachoweza kudhibitiwa.

Fourth, preparation provides direction. Extemporaneous preaching tends to wander. The preacher may set off in one direction in his introduction and end up somewhere quite different. He chases a rabbit and never recovers the scent of his original quarry. An outline gives the sermon a destination and keeps the preacher walking toward it.

Nne, maandalizi hutoa mwelekeo. Kuhubiri bila kujiandaa (papo kwa papo) huelekea kutangatanga. Mhubiri anaweza kuanza kuelekea upande mmoja katika utangulizi wake na kuishia mahali tofauti kabisa. Anamfukuza sungura mwingine na kamwe harudi kwenye harufu ya windo lake la awali. Muhtasari huyapa mahubiri mahali pa kufikia na humfanya mhubiri aendelee kutembea kuelekea huko.

Fifth, preparation allows the Holy Spirit to work over an extended period. If the Spirit can give us a word to speak in the moment we stand to preach, He can do even more if we have given Him a week to shape our thoughts. Preparation does not compete with the Spirit's power; it gives the Spirit room to work in us before we work in the pulpit.

Tano, maandalizi humpa Roho Mtakatifu nafasi ya kufanya kazi kwa muda mrefu. Ikiwa Roho anaweza kutupa neno la kusema saa ile tunaposimama kuhubiri, anaweza kufanya hata zaidi ikiwa tumempa juma zima kuyaunda mawazo yetu. Maandalizi hayashindani na uweza wa Roho; yanampa Roho nafasi ya kufanya kazi ndani yetu kabla sisi hatujafanya kazi mimbarini.
1.3 The Sermon as a House
1.3 Mahubiri Kama Nyumba

It helps to think of a sermon as a house under construction. The text is the foundation — because it is the Word of God, it provides the stability that holds the whole sermon up. The introduction is the entryway: it leads people into the sermon, and like the entryway of a house, it should be relatively small, because no one is supposed to spend much of his life there. The divisions of the sermon are the support beams; their function is to hold the structure up, not to be admired in themselves. The illustrations are the windows that let light in. The conclusion is the exit. Each part is built with care because no part can be left to chance.

Inasaidia kufikiria mahubiri kama nyumba inayojengwa. Kifungu ndicho msingi — kwa sababu ni Neno la Mungu, kinatoa uthabiti unaoshikilia mahubiri yote. Utangulizi ni ukumbi wa kuingilia: unawaongoza watu kuingia katika mahubiri, na kama ukumbi wa kuingilia wa nyumba, unapaswa kuwa mdogo kiasi, kwa sababu hakuna mtu anayetakiwa kutumia sehemu kubwa ya maisha yake hapo. Migawanyo ya mahubiri ni boriti za kutegemeza; kazi yake ni kushikilia jengo, si kustaajabiwa yenyewe. Vielelezo ni madirisha yanayoingiza nuru. Hitimisho ni mlango wa kutokea. Kila sehemu hujengwa kwa uangalifu kwa sababu hakuna sehemu inayoweza kuachwa kwa bahati.

The foundational materials of every unified sermon are six: the text, the idea, the probing question, the keyword, the subject, and the objective. In this unit you learn to use the text. In the units that follow, you will learn to use the others. By the end of Unit 2 you will have all six in hand, and from Unit 3 onward you will use them to construct outlines.

Vifaa vya msingi vya kila mahubiri yenye umoja ni sita: kifungu, wazo, swali la uchunguzi, neno kiini, somo, na lengo. Katika sehemu hii unajifunza kutumia kifungu. Katika sehemu zinazofuata, utajifunza kutumia vingine. Kufikia mwisho wa Sehemu ya 2 utakuwa na vyote sita mkononi, na kuanzia Sehemu ya 3 na kuendelea utavitumia kujenga mihtasari.
1.4 The Text: Laying the Foundation
1.4 Kifungu: Kuweka Msingi

The literal meaning of the word text is "to weave." The text is the fabric on which the sermon is fashioned. Since the time of Origen in the third century, Christian preaching has been derived from a text — but having a text does not by itself guarantee that the preacher has submitted his mind to the Bible. H. H. Farmer warned against the danger that a preacher will use "the scripture words merely as a perch on which his own ideas, like a lot of twittering birds, may alight and preen themselves." The theme of the text and the theme of the sermon must be the same.

Maana halisi ya neno text (kifungu) ni "kufuma." Kifungu ni kitambaa ambacho juu yake mahubiri hutengenezwa. Tangu wakati wa Origen katika karne ya tatu, mahubiri ya Kikristo yametokana na kifungu — lakini kuwa na kifungu peke yake hakuhakikishi kwamba mhubiri ameitiisha akili yake kwa Biblia. H. H. Farmer alionya juu ya hatari kwamba mhubiri atatumia "maneno ya Maandiko kama kitulio tu, ambapo mawazo yake mwenyewe, kama kundi la ndege wanaolialia, yanaweza kutua na kujipamba." Dhamira ya kifungu na dhamira ya mahubiri lazima ziwe moja.

Some years ago I heard a pastor preach from Psalm 142:4 — David, depressed and despondent, writing from a cave: "no man cared for my soul." The pastor preached on "those who care about lost souls," and went through Father, Son, Spirit, heaven, and hell as those who care. The sermon was Biblical and useful — but it had nothing to do with the text. The pastor needed a different text, because his theme and the theme of Psalm 142 simply did not match. Compare that with an outline I once heard from Isaiah 6:1–8 on "visions in an encounter with God": (1) a vision of God, (2) a vision of inadequacy, (3) a vision of service. There the theme of the text and the theme of the sermon were one and the same.

Miaka kadhaa iliyopita nilimsikia mchungaji akihubiri kutoka Zaburi 142:4 — Daudi, akiwa amevunjika moyo na kukata tamaa, akiandika kutoka pangoni: "Hakuna wa kunitunza roho yangu." Mchungaji huyo alihubiri juu ya "wale wanaojali roho zilizopotea," akapitia Baba, Mwana, Roho, mbingu, na kuzimu kama wale wanaojali. Mahubiri yalikuwa ya Kibiblia na yenye manufaa — lakini hayakuwa na uhusiano wowote na kifungu. Mchungaji alihitaji kifungu kingine, kwa sababu dhamira yake na dhamira ya Zaburi 142 hazikulingana kabisa. Linganisha hilo na muhtasari niliousikia wakati mmoja kutoka Isaya 6:1–8 juu ya "maono katika kukutana na Mungu": (1) maono ya Mungu, (2) maono ya kutotosha, (3) maono ya huduma. Hapo dhamira ya kifungu na dhamira ya mahubiri zilikuwa moja na ile ile.
1.5 Seven Methods of Text Selection
1.5 Njia Saba za Kuchagua Kifungu
There are seven distinct methods by which a preacher may select a text. Each is legitimate; the choice depends on the occasion, the congregation, and the gift of the preacher.
Kuna njia saba tofauti ambazo kwazo mhubiri anaweza kuchagua kifungu. Kila moja ni halali; uchaguzi unategemea tukio, kusanyiko, na karama ya mhubiri.

1. Preach on a whole book. It is possible to preach a single sermon on an entire book of the Bible, especially shorter ones — Genesis, Ruth, Jonah, Job, Esther. When you do, select a summary verse to read as the scripture lesson. Eric Hayden in Preaching Through the Bible gives a one-word summary, a theme, and a central verse for every book. For Ephesians he uses the word church, the verse Ephesians 5:30 ("we are members of his body"), and the theme "the essential character of the church." From this he develops three points: the church as intimate relationship, vital union, and loving possession.

1. Hubiri juu ya kitabu kizima. Inawezekana kuhubiri mahubiri moja juu ya kitabu kizima cha Biblia, hasa vitabu vifupi — Mwanzo, Ruthu, Yona, Ayubu, Esta. Unapofanya hivyo, chagua mstari wa muhtasari wa kusoma kama somo la Maandiko. Eric Hayden katika kitabu Preaching Through the Bible (Kuhubiri Katika Biblia Yote) anatoa muhtasari wa neno moja, dhamira, na mstari mkuu kwa kila kitabu. Kwa Waefeso anatumia neno kanisa, mstari wa Waefeso 5:30 ("tu viungo vya mwili wake"), na dhamira "tabia ya msingi ya kanisa." Kutokana na hayo anaendeleza hoja tatu: kanisa kama uhusiano wa karibu, muungano hai, na milki ya upendo.

2. Preach on a chapter. Many chapters in the Bible are excellent material for a single sermon: Genesis 3, Psalm 1, Psalm 22, Psalm 23, Psalm 119, Isaiah 53, John 3, John 10, 1 Corinthians 13, Hebrews 11. A sermon from Hebrews 11 might examine "examples of faith." A summary verse may serve as the scripture lesson, instead of reading the whole chapter aloud.

2. Hubiri juu ya sura. Sura nyingi katika Biblia ni malighafi bora kwa mahubiri moja: Mwanzo 3, Zaburi 1, Zaburi 22, Zaburi 23, Zaburi 119, Isaya 53, Yohana 3, Yohana 10, 1 Wakorintho 13, Waebrania 11. Mahubiri kutoka Waebrania 11 yanaweza kuchunguza "mifano ya imani." Mstari wa muhtasari unaweza kutumika kama somo la Maandiko, badala ya kuisoma sura nzima kwa sauti.

3. Preach on a theme. Much doctrinal preaching is thematic rather than expository — the preacher uses verses gathered from across the Bible to develop a single doctrine. New Testament preaching itself was largely thematic: the kerygma, the Cross, judgment, the love of God. Themes might include grace, the Lordship of Christ, baptism, stewardship, the authority of Scripture, the security of the believer, the fellowship of the church, or the attributes of God (omniscience, omnipotence, omnipresence).

3. Hubiri juu ya dhamira. Mahubiri mengi ya kimafundisho ni ya kidhamira badala ya kufafanua kifungu kimoja — mhubiri anatumia mistari iliyokusanywa kutoka sehemu mbalimbali za Biblia ili kuendeleza fundisho moja. Mahubiri ya Agano Jipya yenyewe kwa sehemu kubwa yalikuwa ya kidhamira: kerygma (tangazo la Injili), Msalaba, hukumu, upendo wa Mungu. Dhamira zinaweza kujumuisha neema, Ubwana wa Kristo, ubatizo, uwakili, mamlaka ya Maandiko, usalama wa mwamini, ushirika wa kanisa, au sifa za Mungu (ujuzi wa yote, uweza wote, kuwapo kila mahali).

4. Preach on a word. A single word can carry an entire sermon. Words like sin, forgiveness, repentance, judgment, reconciliation, or love each contain enough theological weight to support a full message. The Greek word doulos ("bondservant") is what James calls himself in James 1:1; William Barclay's analysis of doulos develops four implications: absolute obedience, absolute humility, absolute loyalty, and absolute pride. When you do a word study, you do not need to use the Greek or Hebrew form in the pulpit. The congregation has little interest in the original word itself; they care about what the word means and how it lands in their lives.

4. Hubiri juu ya neno. Neno moja linaweza kubeba mahubiri yote. Maneno kama dhambi, msamaha, toba, hukumu, upatanisho, au upendo kila moja lina uzito wa kitheolojia wa kutosha kutegemeza ujumbe kamili. Neno la Kigiriki doulos ("mtumwa") ndilo ambalo Yakobo anajiita katika Yakobo 1:1; uchambuzi wa William Barclay juu ya doulos unaendeleza maana nne: utii kamili, unyenyekevu kamili, uaminifu kamili, na fahari kamili. Unapofanya uchunguzi wa neno, huhitaji kutumia umbo la Kigiriki au la Kiebrania mimbarini. Kusanyiko halina hamu kubwa na neno la asili lenyewe; wanajali neno hilo lina maana gani na jinsi linavyogusa maisha yao.

5. Preach on a miracle or a parable. Someone defined the parable as "an earthly story with a heavenly meaning." The New Testament records as many as seventy parables of Jesus; about a third of His teaching is in parable form. Miracles can be handled like enacted parables — there are spiritual truths within the incident itself. The Sower, the Hidden Treasure, the Pearl of Great Price, the Unmerciful Servant, the Good Samaritan, the Rich Fool, the Prodigal Son — each is a sermon waiting to be preached. So is the healing of the blind man in John 9, or Jesus' calming of the storm in Matthew 8.

5. Hubiri juu ya muujiza au mfano. Mtu mmoja alifafanua mfano kuwa "hadithi ya kidunia yenye maana ya kimbingu." Agano Jipya linaandika hadi mifano sabini ya Yesu; karibu theluthi moja ya mafundisho yake iko katika muundo wa mifano. Miujiza inaweza kushughulikiwa kama mifano iliyotendeka — kuna kweli za kiroho ndani ya tukio lenyewe. Mpanzi, Hazina Iliyofichwa, Lulu ya Thamani Kubwa, Mtumwa Asiye na Huruma, Msamaria Mwema, Tajiri Mpumbavu, Mwana Mpotevu — kila mmoja ni mahubiri yanayosubiri kuhubiriwa. Vivyo hivyo kuponywa kwa kipofu katika Yohana 9, au Yesu kutuliza dhoruba katika Mathayo 8.

6. Preach on a character. People are genuinely interested in the lives of other people. The Bible offers characters in vast variety. Some, like Demas or Enoch, have only a few lines written about them; others, like Abraham or Moses, have many chapters. There are characters who inspire (Barnabas) and characters who warn (Absalom, Judas). There are saints and scoundrels, great loves and great hates. Drawing pastoral lessons from the lives of Biblical personalities is one of the easiest forms of preaching, and one of the most engaging for the congregation.

6. Hubiri juu ya mhusika. Watu kwa kweli wanavutiwa na maisha ya watu wengine. Biblia inatoa wahusika wa aina nyingi mno. Baadhi yao, kama Dema au Henoko, wameandikiwa mistari michache tu; wengine, kama Ibrahimu au Musa, wana sura nyingi. Kuna wahusika wanaotutia moyo (Barnaba) na wahusika wanaotuonya (Absalomu, Yuda). Kuna watakatifu na waovu, mapenzi makuu na chuki kuu. Kutoa mafundisho ya kichungaji kutoka katika maisha ya watu wa Biblia ni mojawapo ya njia rahisi zaidi za kuhubiri, na mojawapo ya zinazovutia zaidi kwa kusanyiko.

7. Preach consecutively after doing an analysis. A preaching analysis is the work of moving through a book or section of the Bible in advance, discovering the outlines that the Scripture itself naturally contains. From this analysis you can plan a series of consecutive sermons through the book. The advantage is that you preach the whole counsel of God rather than only your favorite passages, and much of the preparation is done in advance. The disadvantage is that consecutive preaching requires discipline; the preacher must follow the text rather than his own moods. Consecutive analysis will be examined more fully in a later unit.

7. Hubiri kwa mfululizo baada ya kufanya uchambuzi. Uchambuzi wa kuhubiri ni kazi ya kupitia kitabu au sehemu ya Biblia mapema, ukigundua mihtasari ambayo Maandiko yenyewe yanayo kwa asili. Kutokana na uchambuzi huu unaweza kupanga mfululizo wa mahubiri yanayofuatana katika kitabu hicho. Faida yake ni kwamba unahubiri shauri lote la Mungu badala ya vifungu unavyovipenda tu, na sehemu kubwa ya maandalizi hufanyika mapema. Hasara yake ni kwamba kuhubiri kwa mfululizo kunahitaji nidhamu; mhubiri lazima afuate kifungu badala ya hisia zake mwenyewe. Uchambuzi wa mfululizo utachunguzwa kwa kina zaidi katika sehemu ya baadaye.

The Four Purposes of Preaching
Makusudi Manne ya Kuhubiri

You have learned a method. The same sermon, built the same way, may be preached toward very different ends. What changes from one sermon to the next is not the craft in your hands but the purpose in your heart. Across the centuries the Christian pulpit has served four great purposes — to teach, to convert, to heal, and to confront.

Umejifunza njia. Hotuba ile ile ya mahubiri, iliyojengwa kwa njia ile ile, inaweza kuhubiriwa kuelekea malengo tofauti kabisa. Kinachobadilika kutoka mahubiri moja hadi mengine si ufundi ulio mikononi mwako bali kusudi lililo moyoni mwako. Katika karne zote mimbari ya Kikristo imetumikia makusudi manne makuu — kufundisha, kuongoa, kuponya, na kukabili.
10.1 Purpose and Structure
10.1 Kusudi na Muundo

A method is a tool, and a tool can be turned to more than one task. The Apostle Paul gathered the purposes of preaching when he charged Timothy to "preach the word" and to do it "in season, out of season," to "reprove, rebuke, exhort, with all longsuffering and teaching" (2 Timothy 4:2). In that one verse the sermon both comforts and confronts; it teaches and it pleads. The faithful preacher learns to recognize which purpose a given congregation, text, and hour requires, and to bend his method toward it.

Njia ni chombo, na chombo kinaweza kutumiwa kwa kazi zaidi ya moja. Mtume Paulo aliyakusanya makusudi ya kuhubiri pale alipomwagiza Timotheo "lihubiri neno" na kufanya hivyo "wakati ufaao na wakati usiofaa," "karipia, kemea, onya, kwa uvumilivu wote na mafundisho" (2 Timotheo 4:2). Katika mstari huo mmoja mahubiri yanafariji na pia yanakabili; yanafundisha na pia yanasihi. Mhubiri mwaminifu hujifunza kutambua ni kusudi gani kusanyiko fulani, kifungu fulani, na saa fulani vinahitaji, na kuielekeza njia yake kuelekea kusudi hilo.

These four purposes are a matter of the sermon's aim, not its shape. How a sermon is built — topical, textual, expository, or narrative — is a separate question of structure, and structure has little to do with how biblical a sermon is. Every sermon must be biblical; not every sermon is expository. Here our concern is purpose: why we preach a given message, and what we mean it to accomplish. We will take each of the four in turn.

Makusudi haya manne ni suala la lengo la mahubiri, si umbo lake. Jinsi mahubiri yanavyojengwa — ya kimada, ya kifungu, ya ufafanuzi, au ya masimulizi — ni swali tofauti la muundo, na muundo hauhusiani sana na jinsi mahubiri yalivyo ya kibiblia. Kila mahubiri lazima yawe ya kibiblia; si kila mahubiri ni ya ufafanuzi. Hapa tunashughulikia kusudi: kwa nini tunahubiri ujumbe fulani, na tunakusudia utimize nini. Tutayachukua yale manne moja baada ya jingine.
10.2 Doctrinal Preaching — To Teach
10.2 Mahubiri ya Kimafundisho — Kufundisha

The doctrinal sermon takes a basic Christian belief — the cross, the new birth, justification by faith, the Person of Christ, the resurrection, the last things — and preaches it with a view to gaining understanding and acceptance. Its purpose is not merely to inform the mind but to win the heart's consent and then to govern the life. A great doctrine is laid open, explained in plain words, defended where the hearer's questions or the errors of the age require it, and pressed home until the listener not only grasps the truth but lives by it.

Mahubiri ya kimafundisho huchukua imani ya msingi ya Kikristo — msalaba, kuzaliwa upya, kuhesabiwa haki kwa imani, Nafsi ya Kristo, ufufuo, mambo ya siku za mwisho — na kuihubiri kwa lengo la kupata uelewa na ukubali. Kusudi lake si kuiarifu akili tu bali kuupata ukubali wa moyo na kisha kuyaongoza maisha. Fundisho kuu hufunuliwa, hufafanuliwa kwa maneno rahisi, hutetewa pale maswali ya msikilizaji au makosa ya zama yanapohitaji hivyo, na husisitizwa hadi msikilizaji si tu aelewe ukweli bali aishi kwa ukweli huo.

In its structure, doctrinal preaching is usually topical preaching. A great doctrine is rarely confined to a single passage; it is gathered from throughout the Bible — the new birth from John, Romans, and Peter; the atonement from Isaiah, the Gospels, and Hebrews. So the doctrinal sermon collects its truth from many texts and arranges it around one theme, which is exactly what a topical sermon does. This makes it no less biblical than an expository message. Topical, textual, and expository describe how a sermon is arranged, not how faithful it is to Scripture; every sermon must be biblical, but not every sermon need be expository.

Kwa upande wa muundo, mahubiri ya kimafundisho kwa kawaida ni mahubiri ya kimada. Fundisho kuu mara chache hufungwa katika kifungu kimoja tu; hukusanywa kutoka Biblia nzima — kuzaliwa upya kutoka Yohana, Warumi, na Petro; upatanisho kutoka Isaya, Injili, na Waebrania. Kwa hiyo mahubiri ya kimafundisho hukusanya ukweli wake kutoka vifungu vingi na kuupanga kuzunguka wazo moja kuu, jambo ambalo ndilo hasa mahubiri ya kimada hufanya. Hili haliyafanyi kuwa ya kibiblia kidogo kuliko ujumbe wa ufafanuzi. Ya kimada, ya kifungu, na ya ufafanuzi yanaeleza jinsi mahubiri yalivyopangwa, si jinsi yalivyo aminifu kwa Maandiko; kila mahubiri lazima yawe ya kibiblia, lakini si lazima kila mahubiri yawe ya ufafanuzi.

The doctrinal preacher must remember that he is preaching, not lecturing. The constant danger of this kind of sermon is that it hardens into a classroom lesson, as dry as Ezekiel's bones, full of explanation and empty of life. The cure is to keep three things together: make the doctrine clear (take one truth, not ten, and let the whole sermon serve it); make it warm (a doctrine is a window onto the character of God, and should leave the hearer worshiping); and make it applied (every doctrine carries a "therefore" — if Christ is risen, then do not fear the grave). Paul charged Titus to "speak the things which befit the sound doctrine" (Titus 2:1). It is the backbone of a healthy pulpit, and every other purpose depends on it.

Mhubiri wa mafundisho lazima akumbuke kwamba anahubiri, si kutoa mhadhara. Hatari ya kudumu ya aina hii ya mahubiri ni kwamba yanakakamaa na kuwa somo la darasani, makavu kama mifupa ya Ezekieli, yaliyojaa maelezo na yasiyo na uhai. Dawa yake ni kushikilia mambo matatu pamoja: lifanye fundisho liwe wazi (chukua ukweli mmoja, si kumi, na mahubiri yote yautumikie); lifanye liwe na joto (fundisho ni dirisha la kuitazama tabia ya Mungu, na linapaswa kumwacha msikilizaji akiabudu); na lifanye litumike (kila fundisho lina "kwa hiyo" — ikiwa Kristo amefufuka, basi usiliogope kaburi). Paulo alimwagiza Tito, "nena mambo yanayopatana na mafundisho yenye uzima" (Tito 2:1). Ndilo uti wa mgongo wa mimbari yenye afya, na kila kusudi jingine linalitegemea.
10.3 Evangelistic Preaching — To Convert
10.3 Mahubiri ya Kiinjilisti — Kuongoa

The evangelistic sermon proclaims the gospel of Jesus Christ and calls the hearer to a decision. Where the doctrinal sermon labors chiefly for understanding, the evangelistic sermon labors for response. It sets the dark truth of sin against the bright truth of grace, lifts up Christ crucified and risen as the only Savior, and presses the listener to receive him — not someday, but today.

Mahubiri ya kiinjilisti hutangaza injili ya Yesu Kristo na kumwita msikilizaji afanye uamuzi. Pale ambapo mahubiri ya kimafundisho hujitahidi hasa kwa ajili ya uelewa, mahubiri ya kiinjilisti hujitahidi kwa ajili ya mwitikio. Huweka ukweli wa giza wa dhambi dhidi ya ukweli angavu wa neema, humwinua Kristo aliyesulibiwa na kufufuka kama Mwokozi pekee, na humsihi msikilizaji ampokee — si siku moja, bali leo.

Urgency is the mark of this preaching. Paul wrote, "now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation" (2 Corinthians 6:2). The evangelistic preacher believes that every time the gospel is heard a decision is being made, and that there is no neutral ground. He warms the heart, he reasons with the will, and he does not leave the sermon without a clear and earnest invitation; the whole message rises toward that appeal as toward its summit. Felix trembled under Paul's reasoning of righteousness, temperance, and judgment, yet put off his decision to a more convenient season that never came (Acts 24:25). The evangelist preaches so that his hearers will not make that fatal delay. Every other kind of sermon may borrow this urgency; a doctrinal or pastoral message that ends with a clear call to Christ is the stronger for it.

Uharaka ndio alama ya mahubiri haya. Paulo aliandika, "tazama, wakati uliokubalika ndio sasa; tazama, siku ya wokovu ndiyo sasa" (2 Wakorintho 6:2). Mhubiri wa kiinjilisti anaamini kwamba kila mara injili inaposikika uamuzi unafanywa, na kwamba hakuna eneo la katikati. Huupasha moyo joto, hujadiliana na nia, na haachi mahubiri bila mwaliko ulio wazi na wa dhati; ujumbe wote hupanda kuelekea ombi hilo kama kuelekea kilele chake. Feliki alitetemeka Paulo alipokuwa akihojiana naye habari za haki, na kuwa na kiasi, na hukumu, lakini akauahirisha uamuzi wake hadi wakati unaofaa zaidi ambao haukuja kamwe (Matendo 24:25). Mwinjilisti huhubiri ili wasikilizaji wake wasifanye ucheleweshaji huo wenye mauti. Kila aina nyingine ya mahubiri inaweza kuazima uharaka huu; ujumbe wa kimafundisho au wa kichungaji unaoishia kwa mwito ulio wazi wa kumjia Kristo huwa na nguvu zaidi kwa ajili ya hilo.
10.4 Therapeutic (Pastoral) Preaching — To Heal
10.4 Mahubiri ya Kuponya (ya Kichungaji) — Kuponya

This sermon is called by several names — pastoral preaching, therapeutic preaching, or life-situation preaching — but they all describe the same thing: a sermon that meets people where they hurt and brings the comfort and counsel of God's Word to bear upon a real human need. Where doctrinal preaching begins with a truth and evangelistic preaching with the gospel call, pastoral preaching often begins with a problem — grief, fear, guilt, loneliness, a marriage under strain, a wound that will not close — and then brings Scripture to that need as balm and as guide.

Mahubiri haya huitwa kwa majina kadhaa — mahubiri ya kichungaji, mahubiri ya kuponya, au mahubiri ya hali halisi ya maisha — lakini yote yanaeleza kitu kimoja: mahubiri yanayokutana na watu pale wanapoumia na kuleta faraja na shauri la Neno la Mungu juu ya hitaji halisi la mwanadamu. Pale ambapo mahubiri ya kimafundisho huanza na ukweli na mahubiri ya kiinjilisti huanza na mwito wa injili, mahubiri ya kichungaji mara nyingi huanza na tatizo — huzuni ya msiba, hofu, hatia, upweke, ndoa iliyo katika mvutano, jeraha lisilopona — kisha huleta Maandiko kwa hitaji hilo kama dawa ya kupaka na kama mwongozo.

The warrant for this preaching is the shepherd's heart of God himself, who "healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds" (Psalm 147:3), and of the Lord Jesus, who said, "Come unto me, all ye that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest" (Matthew 11:28). Paul wrote to a grieving church not with platitudes but with the hope of the resurrection, "that ye sorrow not, even as the rest, who have no hope" (1 Thessalonians 4:13). To approach it well, begin with the real situation your people face, name it honestly, and then let the Scripture speak to it — not the other way around. But here is its peril, and it is a serious one: pastoral preaching must never decay into mere self-help or borrowed pop-psychology — comfort without Christ, advice without authority. The world has counsel enough; the people of God need a word from God. Let the sermon meet the need, but let it heal with Scripture and not merely soothe with sentiment.

Kibali cha mahubiri haya ni moyo wa kichungaji wa Mungu mwenyewe, ambaye "huwaponya waliovunjika moyo, na kuziganga jeraha zao" (Zaburi 147:3), na wa Bwana Yesu, aliyesema, "Njoni kwangu, ninyi nyote msumbukao na wenye kulemewa na mizigo, nami nitawapumzisha" (Mathayo 11:28). Paulo aliliandikia kanisa lililokuwa likiomboleza si kwa maneno matupu ya kufariji bali kwa tumaini la ufufuo, "msihuzunike kama wengine wasio na tumaini" (1 Wathesalonike 4:13). Ili kuyaendea vizuri, anza na hali halisi ambayo watu wako wanaikabili, itaje kwa uaminifu, kisha yaache Maandiko yanene juu yake — si kinyume chake. Lakini hapa ndipo hatari yake ilipo, nayo ni hatari kubwa: mahubiri ya kichungaji hayapaswi kamwe kuporomoka kuwa mafundisho matupu ya kujisaidia au saikolojia ya mtaani iliyoazimwa — faraja bila Kristo, ushauri bila mamlaka. Ulimwengu una ushauri wa kutosha; watu wa Mungu wanahitaji neno kutoka kwa Mungu. Mahubiri na yakutane na hitaji, lakini yaponye kwa Maandiko na si kutuliza tu kwa hisia.
10.5 Ethical (Prophetic) Preaching — To Confront
10.5 Mahubiri ya Kimaadili (ya Kinabii) — Kukabili

The ethical sermon — often called prophetic preaching — calls the people of God to righteous living and lays the claims of God's holiness upon their conduct, both personal and public. Where pastoral preaching binds up wounds, ethical preaching probes them; where the one comforts, the other confronts. It names sin plainly, summons the hearer to repentance, and marks out the road of obedience. This is the preaching of the prophets: what does the LORD require of you, asked Micah, but "to do justly, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with thy God" (Micah 6:8)? It is the preaching of John the Baptist, who told the crowds to "bring forth fruit worthy of repentance" (Matthew 3:8). Above all it is pictured in Nathan, who went to a king guilty of adultery and murder and, by a story that disarmed him, brought him at last to the words "Thou art the man" (2 Samuel 12:7).

Mahubiri ya kimaadili — ambayo mara nyingi huitwa mahubiri ya kinabii — huwaita watu wa Mungu kwenye maisha ya haki na huweka madai ya utakatifu wa Mungu juu ya mwenendo wao, wa binafsi na wa hadharani. Pale ambapo mahubiri ya kichungaji huganga majeraha, mahubiri ya kimaadili huyachunguza; pale ambapo moja hufariji, jingine hukabili. Huitaja dhambi waziwazi, humwita msikilizaji kwenye toba, na huionyesha njia ya utii. Haya ndiyo mahubiri ya manabii: BWANA anataka nini kwako, aliuliza Mika, ila "kutenda haki, na kupenda rehema, na kwenda kwa unyenyekevu pamoja na Mungu wako" (Mika 6:8)? Ni mahubiri ya Yohana Mbatizaji, aliyewaambia makutano "zaeni matunda yapasayo toba" (Mathayo 3:8). Zaidi ya yote yanaonyeshwa katika Nathani, aliyemwendea mfalme mwenye hatia ya uzinzi na uuaji na, kwa hadithi iliyomvua kinga zake, akamfikisha hatimaye kwenye maneno "Wewe ndiwe mtu huyo" (2 Samweli 12:7).

Yet ethical preaching has its own danger. It can curdle into mere moralism — a list of duties cut off from the gospel — or into bare social commentary that scolds without saving. The remedy is to root every command in grace. We do not preach righteousness as the way to earn God's favor, but as the glad response of those who have already received it. Law tells us what to do; only the gospel gives us the heart to do it. The ethical sermon presses obedience, but always upon a people first reminded of the mercy that makes obedience possible.

Hata hivyo mahubiri ya kimaadili yana hatari yake yenyewe. Yanaweza kuchacha na kuwa maadili matupu — orodha ya wajibu iliyotengwa na injili — au kuwa maoni matupu ya kijamii yanayokemea bila kuokoa. Dawa yake ni kuipandikiza kila amri katika neema. Hatuhubiri haki kama njia ya kujipatia kibali cha Mungu, bali kama mwitikio wa furaha wa wale ambao tayari wamekipokea. Sheria hutuambia la kufanya; injili peke yake ndiyo hutupa moyo wa kulifanya. Mahubiri ya kimaadili husisitiza utii, lakini daima kwa watu ambao kwanza wamekumbushwa rehema inayofanya utii uwezekane.
10.6 One Method, Many Aims
10.6 Njia Moja, Malengo Mengi

Doctrinal, evangelistic, therapeutic, ethical — to teach, to convert, to heal, to confront. A single sermon will often serve more than one of them at once: a doctrinal message may close with an evangelistic appeal; a pastoral word may carry an ethical edge. The wise preacher knows which purpose his text and his people require, and he bends his craft toward it. The WiseSpeak method you have learned equips you for all four. The skill is the same; what you bring to it is the purpose. Learn to ask, before each sermon, not only "What does this text say?" but "What is this sermon for?"

Ya kimafundisho, ya kiinjilisti, ya kuponya, ya kimaadili — kufundisha, kuongoa, kuponya, kukabili. Mahubiri moja mara nyingi yatatumikia zaidi ya kusudi moja kwa wakati mmoja: ujumbe wa kimafundisho unaweza kuishia kwa ombi la kiinjilisti; neno la kichungaji linaweza kubeba makali ya kimaadili. Mhubiri mwenye hekima anajua ni kusudi gani kifungu chake na watu wake wanahitaji, naye huuelekeza ufundi wake kuelekea kusudi hilo. Njia ya WiseSpeak uliyojifunza inakuandaa kwa yote manne. Ujuzi ni ule ule; unachouleta kwake ni kusudi. Jifunze kuuliza, kabla ya kila mahubiri, si tu "Kifungu hiki kinasema nini?" bali pia "Mahubiri haya ni kwa ajili ya nini?"

Develop an Idea
Endeleza Wazo
Idea, probing question, keyword, subject, objective — the five tools that turn a text into a sermon.
Wazo, swali la uchunguzi, neno kiini, somo, lengo — vifaa vitano vinavyogeuza kifungu kuwa mahubiri.
2.1 The Idea
2.1 Wazo

After you have a text, the next foundational material is the idea. The idea is the general topic of the sermon, and it must come from the Scripture itself. Donald Miller laid down a rule that has shaped a generation of preachers: the theme of the text and the theme of the sermon must be the same. If they are not, the text is no longer a text — it is a pretext, a starting point for the preacher's own thoughts. The idea answers the question, "What is the general topic of this text?"

Baada ya kuwa na kifungu, kifaa kinachofuata cha msingi ni wazo. Wazo ni jambo la jumla linalozungumziwa katika mahubiri, na lazima litoke katika Maandiko yenyewe. Donald Miller aliweka kanuni ambayo imewaunda wahubiri wa kizazi kizima: dhamira ya kifungu na dhamira ya mahubiri lazima ziwe moja. Zisipokuwa moja, kifungu si kifungu tena — ni kisingizio, mahali pa kuanzia tu kwa mawazo ya mhubiri mwenyewe. Wazo hujibu swali, "Kifungu hiki kinazungumzia jambo gani kwa ujumla?"

Examples of an idea include: faith, the kingdom of God, hope, law, grieving the Holy Spirit, works, love, fasting, baptism, singleness, growing, family. Each of these is a real Biblical idea — but each is also far too general to preach in one sermon. Try preaching on faith. You could speak about the qualities of faith, the demands of faith, examples of faith, men of faith, or reasons faith is important — and each of these would itself be a full sermon. The idea is the raw quarry stone. It must be cut down before it can be set in a wall.

Mifano ya wazo ni pamoja na: imani, ufalme wa Mungu, tumaini, sheria, kumhuzunisha Roho Mtakatifu, matendo, upendo, kufunga, ubatizo, useja, kukua, familia. Kila moja ya haya ni wazo halisi la Kibiblia — lakini kila moja pia ni la jumla mno kuhubiriwa katika mahubiri moja. Jaribu kuhubiri juu ya imani. Ungeweza kuzungumzia sifa za imani, madai ya imani, mifano ya imani, watu wa imani, au sababu za imani kuwa muhimu — na kila moja ya hayo lingekuwa mahubiri kamili peke yake. Wazo ni jiwe ghafi la machimbo. Lazima likatwe kwanza kabla halijawekwa ukutani.

The tool that cuts the idea down is the probing question. But before you reach for that tool, you have to have the stone. Open your text and ask the simple question: "What is this passage about?" Whatever single noun or phrase comes back is your idea. Resist the temptation to make it clever. The idea should be plain. Cleverness comes later.

Kifaa kinachokata wazo ni swali la uchunguzi. Lakini kabla hujakishika kifaa hicho, lazima uwe na jiwe. Fungua kifungu chako na uulize swali rahisi: "Kifungu hiki kinahusu nini?" Nomino au kirai chochote kimoja kinachorudi ndicho wazo lako. Pinga kishawishi cha kulifanya liwe la kijanja. Wazo linapaswa kuwa la wazi. Ujanja huja baadaye.
2.2 The Probing Question
2.2 Swali la Uchunguzi

The probing question is the tool that narrows the idea to a manageable size. The news industry uses these same questions to produce a story. Rudyard Kipling wrote a poem in The Elephant's Child that is the easiest way to remember them:

Swali la uchunguzi ni kifaa kinachopunguza wazo hadi ukubwa unaoweza kushughulikiwa. Tasnia ya habari hutumia maswali haya haya kutunga habari. Rudyard Kipling aliandika shairi katika The Elephant's Child (Mtoto wa Tembo) ambalo ndiyo njia rahisi zaidi ya kuyakumbuka:
Kipling's Six Honest Servants I keep six honest serving men They taught me all I knew, Their names are What and Why and When And How and Where and Who.

Watumishi Sita Waaminifu wa Kipling
Nina watumishi sita waaminifu
Walinifundisha yote niliyojua,
Majina yao ni Nini na Kwa nini na Lini
Na Jinsi gani na Wapi na Nani.

For preaching purposes, Kipling's six become eight by adding which and how much. So the eight interrogatives are: who, which, what, why, when, where, how, and how much. The probing question is formed by putting the idea together with one of these interrogatives in a complete sentence question.

Kwa madhumuni ya kuhubiri, viulizi sita vya Kipling vinakuwa vinane kwa kuongeza -pi (ipi/yupi) na kiasi gani. Kwa hiyo viulizi vinane ni: nani, -pi, nini, kwa nini, lini, wapi, jinsi gani, na kiasi gani. Swali la uchunguzi huundwa kwa kuliweka wazo pamoja na mojawapo ya viulizi hivi katika swali lenye sentensi kamili.
Take the idea of hope. Each interrogative produces a different probing question, and each probing question will produce a different sermon:
Chukua wazo la tumaini. Kila kiulizi huzaa swali la uchunguzi tofauti, na kila swali la uchunguzi litazaa mahubiri tofauti:

Who generally points to people. "Who has hope?" Which points to types or kinds. "Which kinds of hope are valid?" What points to steps, ways, or qualities. "What are the values of hope?" Why points to reasons. "Why is hope necessary?" When points to times. "When do we need hope?" Where points to places. "Where do we find hope?" How points to procedures or ways. "How is hope obtained, or lost?" How much points to quantity. "How much hope do we need?"

Nani kwa kawaida huelekeza kwa watu. "Ni nani walio na tumaini?"
-pi (ipi/zipi) huelekeza kwa aina au jamii. "Ni aina zipi za tumaini zilizo halali?"
Nini huelekeza kwa hatua, njia, au sifa. "Ni nini thamani za tumaini?"
Kwa nini huelekeza kwa sababu. "Kwa nini tumaini ni la lazima?"
Lini huelekeza kwa nyakati. "Ni lini tunahitaji tumaini?"
Wapi huelekeza kwa mahali. "Tunapata tumaini wapi?"
Jinsi gani huelekeza kwa taratibu au njia. "Tumaini hupatikanaje, au hupoteaje?"
Kiasi gani huelekeza kwa wingi. "Tunahitaji tumaini kiasi gani?"

Notice that the same idea — hope — has just produced eight different sermons. Each is legitimate. Each is Biblical. Each will require a different sermon outline. The probing question has done the cutting work that the idea alone could not do.

Angalia kwamba wazo lile lile — tumaini — limezaa mahubiri manane tofauti. Kila moja ni halali. Kila moja ni la Kibiblia. Kila moja litahitaji muhtasari tofauti wa mahubiri. Swali la uchunguzi limefanya kazi ya kukata ambayo wazo peke yake lisingeweza kuifanya.
2.3 The Keyword
2.3 Neno Kiini

The keyword arises naturally from the probing question. It is usually a plural noun, and it is the single most important word in your sermon's structure — because the keyword is what unites the outline. Every point of the sermon will be a particular instance of the keyword.

Neno kiini hutokea kwa kawaida kutokana na swali la uchunguzi. Kwa kawaida ni nomino ya wingi, na ndilo neno moja muhimu kuliko yote katika muundo wa mahubiri yako — kwa sababu neno kiini ndilo linalounganisha muhtasari. Kila hoja ya mahubiri itakuwa mfano mmoja mahususi wa neno kiini.

Three rules govern the keyword. First, it is always plural. Almost without exception, your keyword will end in -s. Check yours: if it does not end in -s and is not an irregular plural like "people" or "men," it is probably wrong. Second, only one keyword per sermon. Just as you must use only one interrogative, you must use only one keyword. Third, avoid generic words like "things." "Three things about prayer" is not a keyword; it is laziness. The keyword should be as specific as possible to the actual content of your divisions.

Kanuni tatu huongoza neno kiini. Kwanza, daima liko katika wingi. Karibu bila kukosa, neno lako kiini litakuwa katika umbo la wingi (kwa Kiingereza huishia na -s). Likague lako: ikiwa haliko katika wingi (maneno kiini sahihi ni kama "sababu," "njia," "nyakati," "watu"), huenda si sahihi. Pili, neno kiini moja tu kwa kila mahubiri. Kama vile unavyopaswa kutumia kiulizi kimoja tu, lazima utumie neno kiini moja tu. Tatu, epuka maneno ya jumla kama "mambo." "Mambo matatu kuhusu maombi" si neno kiini; ni uvivu. Neno kiini linapaswa kuwa mahususi kadiri iwezekanavyo kwa maudhui halisi ya migawanyo yako.
Watch how the keyword arises from each probing question on the idea of faith:
Tazama jinsi neno kiini linavyotokea kutokana na kila swali la uchunguzi juu ya wazo la imani:

Who are some people of great faith? Keyword = people. Which are the elements of faith? Keyword = elements. What are the ingredients of faith? Keyword = ingredients. What are the effects of faith? Keyword = effects. (Possible outline: seeing the invisible, doing the impossible, believing the incredible.) Why have faith? Keyword = reasons. (Possible outline: abundant life, eternal life.) When should we have faith? Keyword = times. (When discouraged, when distracted, when disappointed.) Where may faith be found? Keyword = places. (Before the throne, in the closet, near the cross.) How do we show faith? Keyword = ways. (By word, by walk, by witness.) How much faith do we need? Keyword = amounts. (Enough to cover sorrow, enough to fill our lives, enough to overflow into joy.)

Ni akina nani baadhi ya watu wenye imani kubwa? Neno kiini = watu.
Ni vipengele vipi vya imani? Neno kiini = vipengele.
Ni nini viambato vya imani? Neno kiini = viambato.
Ni nini matokeo ya imani? Neno kiini = matokeo. (Muhtasari unaowezekana: kuona yasiyoonekana, kutenda yasiyowezekana, kuamini yasiyoaminika.)
Kwa nini tuwe na imani? Neno kiini = sababu. (Muhtasari unaowezekana: uzima tele, uzima wa milele.)
Ni lini tunapaswa kuwa na imani? Neno kiini = nyakati. (Tunapokata tamaa, tunapovurugwa, tunapovunjika moyo.)
Imani inaweza kupatikana wapi? Neno kiini = mahali. (Mbele ya kiti cha enzi, katika chumba cha siri, karibu na msalaba.)
Tunaonyeshaje imani? Neno kiini = njia. (Kwa neno, kwa mwenendo, kwa ushuhuda.)
Tunahitaji imani kiasi gani? Neno kiini = viwango. (Ya kutosha kufunika huzuni, ya kutosha kujaza maisha yetu, ya kutosha kufurika kuwa furaha.)

2.4 The Subject
2.4 Somo

Having a clear subject is what prevents aimless wandering in preaching. I remember walking through the woods with my father as a boy. I would have been hopelessly lost — every tree looked the same — but my father pulled out his compass at intervals. The compass gave him a fixed point of reference; we did not wander. The subject of a sermon is its compass.

Kuwa na somo lililo wazi ndiko kunakozuia kutangatanga bila lengo katika kuhubiri. Nakumbuka nikitembea msituni pamoja na baba yangu nilipokuwa mvulana. Ningepotea kabisa — kila mti ulionekana sawa — lakini baba yangu alitoa dira yake mara kwa mara. Dira ilimpa mahali pa kudumu pa kurejelea; hatukutangatanga. Somo la mahubiri ndilo dira yake.

The subject is the keyword plus a modifier. A modifier is anything that describes or limits the keyword. Three forms of modifier are common. The first is the adjective: "seven deadly sins" — the words "seven" and "deadly" both modify the keyword "sins." The second is the prepositional phrase: "ways of gaining faith" — the keyword is "ways," and "of gaining faith" is a prepositional phrase that modifies it. The third is the subordinate clause: "qualities that God possesses" — "qualities" is the keyword, and "that God possesses" is a clause that modifies it.

Somo ni neno kiini pamoja na kifafanuzi. Kifafanuzi ni kitu chochote kinachoeleza au kuweka mipaka kwa neno kiini. Aina tatu za kifafanuzi ni za kawaida. Ya kwanza ni kivumishi: "dhambi saba za mauti" — maneno "saba" na "za mauti" yote yanafafanua neno kiini "dhambi." Ya pili ni kirai kihusishi: "njia za kupata imani" — neno kiini ni "njia," na "za kupata imani" ni kirai kihusishi kinachofafanua neno hilo. Ya tatu ni kishazi tegemezi: "sifa ambazo Mungu anazo" — "sifa" ni neno kiini, na "ambazo Mungu anazo" ni kishazi kinachofafanua neno hilo.

The subject answers the question, "What is the sermon about?" If you ask the probing question, "What are some ways of gaining faith?", the keyword is "ways" and the subject is "ways of gaining faith." Each division of the outline will be one specific way of gaining faith. The congregation, when they take notes, will be able to write the subject at the top of their page and write each numbered point underneath. They will know what the sermon is about, and so will you.

Somo hujibu swali, "Mahubiri haya yanahusu nini?" Ukiuliza swali la uchunguzi, "Ni zipi baadhi ya njia za kupata imani?", neno kiini ni "njia" na somo ni "njia za kupata imani." Kila mgawanyo wa muhtasari utakuwa njia moja mahususi ya kupata imani. Kusanyiko, wanapoandika maelezo, wataweza kuandika somo juu ya ukurasa wao na kuandika kila hoja yenye namba chini yake. Watajua mahubiri yanahusu nini, nawe pia utajua.
2.5 The Objective
2.5 Lengo

The objective is the goal of the sermon. It answers the question, "What do I want people to do?" The objective should be phrased as an action, not as a belief or attitude — because beliefs and attitudes will follow when actions are right, but actions will not always follow when beliefs and attitudes are merely informed.

Lengo ni shabaha ya mahubiri. Hujibu swali, "Nataka watu wafanye nini?" Lengo linapaswa kuandikwa kama tendo, si kama imani au mtazamo — kwa sababu imani na mitazamo hufuata matendo yanapokuwa sahihi, lakini matendo hayafuati kila mara imani na mitazamo inapopewa taarifa tu.

A useful formula is to begin the objective with the words "people will…" If your action is salvation, the objective might be: "People will respond during the invitation to receive Christ as Savior." If your subject deals with anger, the objective might be: "People will begin to control their anger during difficult situations." If your subject deals with prayer, the objective might be: "People will set aside a specific time each day for prayer this week." Each of these is concrete, each is measurable, and each gives the conclusion of your sermon a clear destination.

Kanuni moja yenye msaada ni kuanza lengo kwa maneno "Watu wata…" Ikiwa tendo lako ni wokovu, lengo linaweza kuwa: "Watu wataitikia wakati wa mwaliko ili kumpokea Kristo kama Mwokozi." Ikiwa somo lako linahusu hasira, lengo linaweza kuwa: "Watu wataanza kudhibiti hasira yao katika hali ngumu." Ikiwa somo lako linahusu maombi, lengo linaweza kuwa: "Watu watatenga muda maalum kila siku kwa ajili ya maombi juma hili." Kila moja ya haya ni dhahiri, kila moja linapimika, na kila moja linampa hitimisho la mahubiri yako mahali pa kufikia palipo wazi.

When you have completed the five tools of Unit 2 — idea, probing question, keyword, subject, and objective — you have completed the foundation. From Unit 3 forward you will use these foundational materials to construct outlines.

Construct Your Outline
Jenga Muhtasari Wako
Five marks of a good outline, and the deductive method that produces it.
Alama tano za muhtasari mzuri, na njia ya kideduktivu inayouzaa.
3.1 How Many Divisions?
3.1 Migawanyo Mingapi?

Most homiletic writers agree that two to five divisions is the right range for a sermon. Less than two is not enough to develop a theme adequately. More than five becomes too much for the congregation to follow and remember. Three is a classical default, and not without reason. Craig Skinner quotes the limerick that justifies it:

Waandishi wengi wa elimu ya mahubiri (homiletiki) wanakubaliana kwamba migawanyo miwili hadi mitano ndiyo idadi inayofaa kwa mahubiri. Chini ya miwili haitoshi kuendeleza dhamira ipasavyo. Zaidi ya mitano inakuwa mingi mno kwa kusanyiko kuifuata na kuikumbuka. Mitatu ni idadi ya kawaida ya kihistoria, na si bila sababu. Craig Skinner ananukuu shairi fupi la kuchekesha (limerick) linaloihalalisha:
Skinner's limerickThere was a young fellow from Lyme, Who lived with three wives at a time; When they asked, "Why the third?" He replied, "One's absurd; And bigamy, sir, is a crime!"

Shairi fupi la Skinner
Palikuwa na kijana wa mji wa Lyme,
Aliyeishi na wake watatu kwa wakati mmoja;
Walipomwuliza, "Kwa nini wa tatu?"
Akajibu, "Mmoja ni upuuzi;
Na kuoa wawili, bwana, ni kosa la jinai!"

The structure of a sermon deserves more attention than most preachers give it. Some homiletic writers advise: "Don't make the outline obtrusive." I have never been able to imagine an outline that was too noticeable. An old bony cow may not be pretty, but it is still preferable to a cow lying dead in the field with no bones at all. Some of the most effective preachers in history made their outlines visible — they not only stated each point but repeated the whole outline at the start of every new section. The congregation came away knowing exactly what they had heard.

Muundo wa mahubiri unastahili uangalifu zaidi kuliko ule ambao wahubiri wengi huupa. Baadhi ya waandishi wa elimu ya mahubiri hushauri: "Usiufanye muhtasari uonekane waziwazi mno." Sijawahi kuweza kuwaza muhtasari ulioonekana kupita kiasi. Ng'ombe mzee aliyekonda mpaka mifupa ikaonekana huenda asiwe mrembo, lakini bado ni bora kuliko ng'ombe aliyelala amekufa shambani bila mifupa yoyote. Baadhi ya wahubiri wenye matokeo makubwa zaidi katika historia waliifanya mihtasari yao ionekane — hawakutaja tu kila hoja bali walirudia muhtasari mzima mwanzoni mwa kila sehemu mpya. Kusanyiko liliondoka likijua hasa walichokisikia.
3.2 Five Marks of a Good Outline
3.2 Alama Tano za Muhtasari Mzuri
A well-built outline shows five characteristics. They function together; weakness in any one of them will weaken the whole sermon.
Muhtasari uliojengwa vizuri huonyesha sifa tano. Zinafanya kazi pamoja; udhaifu katika mojawapo utadhoofisha mahubiri yote.

1. Unity. The whole sermon is about one thing — not three things, not five things, but one. Unity is the most important of the five marks because without it nothing else will hold. The keyword is your main tool for unity; every division must be a particular instance of the keyword. Consider this poor outline: (I) All Christians need to pray; (II) The Psalms lead us to praise God's holy name; (III) Some other remarks about prayer. Three points, all about prayer in some way, but disjointed — there is no real subject. The outline could be repaired by selecting a clear subject like "necessities in prayer," and arranging the points beneath it: (I) the need to request, (II) the need to praise, (III) the need to confess.

1. Umoja. Mahubiri yote yanahusu jambo moja — si mambo matatu, si mambo matano, bali moja. Umoja ndio muhimu zaidi kati ya alama hizo tano kwa sababu bila huo hakuna kingine kitakachoshikamana. Neno kiini ndicho chombo chako kikuu cha umoja; kila mgawanyo lazima uwe mfano mahususi wa neno kiini. Fikiria muhtasari huu dhaifu: (I) Wakristo wote wanahitaji kuomba; (II) Zaburi zinatuongoza kulisifu jina takatifu la Mungu; (III) Maelezo mengine kuhusu maombi. Hoja tatu, zote zinahusu maombi kwa namna fulani, lakini hazijaunganika — hakuna somo halisi. Muhtasari huu ungeweza kurekebishwa kwa kuchagua somo lililo wazi kama "mahitaji katika maombi," na kupanga hoja chini yake: (I) hitaji la kuomba (kuleta maombi yetu), (II) hitaji la kusifu, (III) hitaji la kuungama.

2. Order. Order is the relationship of the parts to each other and to the whole. Each division should be distinct from the others, and none should be equal to the subject. Take 2 Corinthians 13:14: "The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Spirit, be with you all." A subject like "the blessings we receive from God" will produce a flawed outline because the second division ("the love of God") repeats the word God already in the subject. A better subject is "the blessings we receive from the Trinity," which yields a polished outline: (I) the grace of the Son, (II) the love of the Father, (III) the fellowship of the Spirit.

2. Mpangilio. Mpangilio ni uhusiano wa sehemu zenyewe kwa zenyewe na kwa jumla nzima. Kila mgawanyo unapaswa kuwa tofauti na mingine, na hakuna unaopaswa kuwa sawa na somo. Chukua 2 Wakorintho 13:14: "Neema ya Bwana Yesu Kristo, na pendo la Mungu, na ushirika wa Roho Mtakatifu, ziwe pamoja nanyi nyote." Somo kama "baraka tunazopokea kutoka kwa Mungu" litazaa muhtasari wenye kasoro kwa sababu mgawanyo wa pili ("pendo la Mungu") unarudia neno Mungu ambalo tayari limo katika somo. Somo bora zaidi ni "baraka tunazopokea kutoka kwa Utatu," ambalo linatoa muhtasari ulio nadhifu: (I) neema ya Mwana, (II) pendo la Baba, (III) ushirika wa Roho.

3. Movement. The outline goes somewhere. There is a clear starting point and an identifiable destination. Edgar Jackson observed: "Contrary to generally accepted practice, it is psychologically sound to make your strongest point first." Lost attention is hard to regain. At the same time, it is wise to put the most evangelistic point last, because the sermon will move into the invitation from there, and an evangelistic peak makes the transition natural. A useful pattern is: (I) a strong point to gain attention, (II) a sustaining point that keeps attention, (III) the most evangelistic point, leading into the invitation.

3. Mwendo. Muhtasari unaelekea mahali fulani. Kuna mahali pa kuanzia palipo wazi na mwisho unaotambulika. Edgar Jackson aliona hivi: "Kinyume na desturi inayokubaliwa na wengi, ni sahihi kisaikolojia kuweka hoja yako yenye nguvu zaidi kwanza." Usikivu uliopotea ni vigumu kuurudisha. Wakati huohuo, ni busara kuweka hoja yenye msisitizo mkubwa zaidi wa kiinjilisti mwishoni, kwa sababu mahubiri yataingia katika mwaliko kutoka hapo, na kilele cha kiinjilisti hufanya mpito huo uwe wa kawaida. Mtindo unaofaa ni huu: (I) hoja yenye nguvu ya kuvuta usikivu, (II) hoja ya kudumisha usikivu, (III) hoja yenye msisitizo mkubwa zaidi wa kiinjilisti, inayoongoza katika mwaliko.

4. Proportion. The divisions are roughly equal in length and weight. The temptation is to lavish ninety percent of the sermon on the first point and rush through the others — the tail wagging the dog. If a point is important enough to make, it deserves to be developed. If it cannot be developed, perhaps it should not be a separate point at all.

4. Uwiano. Migawanyo inakaribiana kwa urefu na kwa uzito. Kishawishi ni kumwaga asilimia tisini ya mahubiri juu ya hoja ya kwanza na kukimbia haraka katika zile nyingine — mkia ukimtikisa mbwa. Ikiwa hoja ni muhimu kiasi cha kutajwa, inastahili kuendelezwa. Ikiwa haiwezi kuendelezwa, labda haipaswi kuwa hoja inayojitegemea hata kidogo.

5. Parallelism. The divisions match each other in grammatical structure. If the first division is a phrase, all the others should be phrases — not sentences or single words. Verbs should be active rather than passive where possible. Take a flawed outline from Matthew 14:14–21 on "Ways Jesus demonstrates His compassion": (I) Jesus healed their sick, (II) They were shown love by Him, (III) They were fed by Him. Two of the three are passive. Recast in active and parallel form: (I) He healed them, (II) He loved them, (III) He fed them. The three lines now sound like three lines, and the congregation will remember them.

5. Ulinganifu. Migawanyo inalingana kwa muundo wa kisarufi. Ikiwa mgawanyo wa kwanza ni kirai, mingine yote inapaswa kuwa virai — si sentensi wala maneno mamoja mamoja. Vitenzi vinapaswa kuwa katika kauli ya kutenda badala ya kauli ya kutendwa inapowezekana. Chukua muhtasari wenye kasoro kutoka Mathayo 14:14–21 juu ya "Njia ambazo Yesu anaonyesha huruma yake": (I) Yesu aliwaponya wagonjwa wao, (II) Walionyeshwa upendo naye, (III) Walilishwa naye. Hoja mbili kati ya tatu ziko katika kauli ya kutendwa. Ziandike upya katika muundo wa kutenda na unaolingana: (I) Aliwaponya, (II) Aliwapenda, (III) Aliwalisha. Mistari hiyo mitatu sasa inasikika kama mistari mitatu inayoendana, na kusanyiko litaikumbuka.

Do not force alliteration onto a text it will not bear. Many a fine outline has been ruined by a preacher who insisted that every point begin with the same letter and ended up bending the meaning of the text to do it. Parallelism in grammar is helpful; alliteration is sometimes helpful but never required.

Usilazimishe kufanana kwa sauti za mwanzo (aliterasi) juu ya kifungu kisichoweza kukibeba. Mihtasari mingi mizuri imeharibiwa na mhubiri aliyeshikilia kwamba kila hoja ianze kwa herufi ileile, na mwishowe akapotosha maana ya kifungu ili kufanikisha hilo. Ulinganifu wa kisarufi unasaidia; aliterasi wakati mwingine inasaidia lakini haihitajiki kamwe.
3.3 The Deductive Method
3.3 Njia ya Kideduktivu

There are two principal ways of building a sermon outline: deduction and induction. This unit covers deduction; Unit 4 will cover induction. Deduction is reasoning from the general to the specific. You begin with a general statement — for example, "God is great" — and then point out specific ways that statement is true: (I) great in His knowledge, (II) great in His power, (III) great in His presence. The general is broken down into the specific.

Kuna njia mbili kuu za kujenga muhtasari wa mahubiri: udeduktivu na uinduktivu. Sehemu hii inashughulikia udeduktivu; Sehemu ya 4 itashughulikia uinduktivu. Udeduktivu ni kufikiri kutoka kwa jumla hadi kwa mahususi (kutoka kanuni hadi mifano). Unaanza na kauli ya jumla — kwa mfano, "Mungu ni mkuu" — kisha unaonyesha njia mahususi ambazo kauli hiyo ni kweli: (I) mkuu katika ujuzi wake, (II) mkuu katika uweza wake, (III) mkuu katika uwepo wake. Jambo la jumla linagawanywa katika mambo mahususi.

In preaching, deduction works like this: after discovering the idea contained in your text and forming a subject, you state the subject as a general truth and then list specific instances of it. Each point is a subdivision of the larger subject. Topical preaching is almost always deductive, but expository preaching often uses deduction as well — the preacher takes a verse, identifies its main affirmation, and then walks through the specific ways it is true.

Katika kuhubiri, udeduktivu hufanya kazi hivi: baada ya kugundua wazo lililomo katika kifungu chako na kuunda somo, unalitaja somo kama kweli ya jumla kisha unaorodhesha mifano mahususi yake. Kila hoja ni mgawanyo mdogo wa somo lililo kubwa zaidi. Mahubiri ya kimada karibu kila mara ni ya kideduktivu, lakini mahubiri ya kifafanuzi (expository) mara nyingi hutumia udeduktivu pia — mhubiri anachukua mstari, anatambua tamko lake kuu, kisha anapitia njia mahususi ambazo tamko hilo ni kweli.

I once preached a message called "Christ Across Canada" using Luke 19:39–40, where Jesus told the crowds that if His followers were silent, the very stones would cry out. My idea was that nature itself declares the name of Christ. My subject was "reminders of the name of Christ throughout Canada." Using deduction, the four points became:

Wakati mmoja nilihubiri ujumbe ulioitwa "Kristo Katika Kanada Yote" nikitumia Luka 19:39–40, ambapo Yesu aliwaambia makutano kwamba wafuasi wake wakinyamaza, mawe yenyewe yatapiga kelele. Wazo langu lilikuwa kwamba maumbile yenyewe yanalitangaza jina la Kristo. Somo langu lilikuwa "vikumbusho vya jina la Kristo kote Kanada." Kwa kutumia udeduktivu, hoja nne zilikuwa hizi:

(I) He is the Living Water at Niagara (John 4:10). (II) He is the Bread of Life through the plains (John 6:35). (III) He is the Solid Rock on the mountains (1 Corinthians 10:4). (IV) He is the True Vine in the Okanagan Valley (John 15:5).

(I) Yeye ndiye Maji Yaliyo Hai huko Niagara (Yohana 4:10).
(II) Yeye ndiye Chakula cha Uzima katika nyanda za tambarare (Yohana 6:35).
(III) Yeye ndiye Mwamba Imara juu ya milima (1 Wakorintho 10:4).
(IV) Yeye ndiye Mzabibu wa Kweli katika Bonde la Okanagan (Yohana 15:5).

Notice that every point has a Scripture reference. This is the rule for deductive preaching: every point must be supported by a verse. If you cannot find a verse to support a point, you should not preach the point. The preacher's authority is the Word of God, and the moment he begins making points the Bible does not make, he has stepped outside that authority.

Angalia kwamba kila hoja ina rejeo la Maandiko. Hii ndiyo kanuni ya mahubiri ya kideduktivu: kila hoja lazima iungwe mkono na mstari wa Biblia. Ikiwa huwezi kupata mstari wa kuiunga mkono hoja, hupaswi kuihubiri hoja hiyo. Mamlaka ya mhubiri ni Neno la Mungu, na pale tu anapoanza kutoa hoja ambazo Biblia haitoi, ametoka nje ya mamlaka hayo.
3.4 The Topical Sermon
3.4 Mahubiri ya Kimada

A topical sermon takes its idea from a text but draws its supporting material from across the Bible. Many doctrinal sermons are topical because doctrine is rarely confined to a single passage. Many of the sermons Jesus preached were topical in form. The topical sermon can be just as Biblical as the expository — provided that every point is anchored in a verse.

Mahubiri ya kimada huchukua wazo lake kutoka katika kifungu lakini huchota vifaa vyake vya kuunga mkono kutoka kote katika Biblia. Mahubiri mengi ya kimafundisho ni ya kimada kwa sababu fundisho mara chache hufungwa katika kifungu kimoja tu. Mahubiri mengi aliyoyahubiri Yesu yalikuwa ya kimada kwa muundo wake. Mahubiri ya kimada yanaweza kuwa ya Kibiblia sawasawa na yale ya kifafanuzi — mradi kila hoja imetiwa nanga katika mstari wa Biblia.
A Good Friday sermon I have preached more than once is "The Seven Words of the Cross." Its idea is the Cross; its keyword is "words"; its subject is "the seven words of the Cross." The outline runs:

Mahubiri ya Ijumaa Kuu ambayo nimeyahubiri zaidi ya mara moja ni "Maneno Saba ya Msalaba." Wazo lake ni Msalaba; neno kiini lake ni "maneno"; somo lake ni "maneno saba ya Msalaba." Muhtasari unakwenda hivi:

(I) A word of pardon (Luke 23:34) — "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do." (II) A word of promise (Luke 23:39–43) — "Today shalt thou be with me in Paradise." (III) A word of provision (John 19:26–27) — "Behold thy son… behold thy mother." (IV) A word of pain (John 19:28–29) — "I thirst." (V) A word of dereliction (Matthew 27:46) — "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?" (VI) A word of triumph (John 19:30) — "It is finished." (VII) A word of commitment (Luke 23:46) — "Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit."

(I) Neno la msamaha (Luka 23:34) — "Baba, uwasamehe, kwa kuwa hawajui watendalo."
(II) Neno la ahadi (Luka 23:39–43) — "Leo hivi utakuwa pamoja nami peponi."
(III) Neno la kuwatunza wake (Yohana 19:26–27) — "Mama, tazama, mwanao!… Tazama, mama yako!"
(IV) Neno la maumivu (Yohana 19:28–29) — "Naona kiu."
(V) Neno la kuachwa (Mathayo 27:46) — "Mungu wangu, Mungu wangu, mbona umeniacha?"
(VI) Neno la ushindi (Yohana 19:30) — "Imekwisha."
(VII) Neno la kujikabidhi (Luka 23:46) — "Baba, mikononi mwako naiweka roho yangu."

Seven points violates the normal rule of three to five, and indeed when I preach this sermon I do not use subpoints. As a general principle, when a sermon has more than three points, drop the subpoints. The congregation cannot hold both a long outline and a layered one in their heads at the same time.

Hoja saba zinavunja kanuni ya kawaida ya hoja tatu hadi tano, na kwa kweli ninapohubiri mahubiri haya situmii hoja ndogo. Kama kanuni ya jumla, mahubiri yanapokuwa na hoja zaidi ya tatu, ziondoe hoja ndogo. Kusanyiko haliwezi kushika kichwani kwa wakati mmoja muhtasari mrefu na muhtasari wenye matabaka mengi.

Njia ya Jeopardy katika kuhubiri — jibu limetolewa ndani ya kifungu, na kazi yako ni kugundua swali. Uinduktivu, mahubiri ya kifungu, na mahubiri ya kifafanuzi.
4.1 Why Two Days on Induction
4.1 Kwa Nini Siku Mbili kwa Uinduktivu

In my experience, students have had more difficulty grasping the inductive method of sermon outlining than any other part of this course. For that reason I am giving you two days to work on induction and two days to work on the textual method. Read the material on the first day and complete one outline. On day two, reread the material and complete any additional outlines called for in the activity. Repeat the same procedure for days three and four. Take it slowly. The technique looks simple once you have it, but it is built upside-down from what most beginning preachers expect, and that takes some getting used to.

Kwa uzoefu wangu, wanafunzi wamepata ugumu zaidi kuielewa njia ya kiinduktivu ya kuandaa muhtasari wa mahubiri kuliko sehemu nyingine yoyote ya kozi hii. Kwa sababu hiyo ninakupa siku mbili za kufanyia kazi uinduktivu na siku mbili za kufanyia kazi njia ya kifungu. Soma maelezo siku ya kwanza na ukamilishe muhtasari mmoja. Siku ya pili, soma tena maelezo na ukamilishe mihtasari mingine yoyote inayotakiwa katika zoezi. Rudia utaratibu huohuo kwa siku ya tatu na ya nne. Nenda polepole. Mbinu hii inaonekana rahisi ukishaipata, lakini imejengwa kinyume kabisa na kile ambacho wahubiri wengi wanaoanza wanatarajia, na hilo huchukua muda kulizoea.
4.2 D. Induction
4.2 D. Uinduktivu

Another way of forming an outline is through induction. Induction is a type of reasoning which begins with the specific and moves to the general — the opposite approach to deduction. It is possible to observe the mountains, the stars, and the seas, and then conclude that there must be an awesome God who created them. One looks at specific examples and forms a general conclusion. In preaching, you begin with the points found in a text and work backward to form a subject. This is used for producing both textual and expository sermons. The process is something like the Jeopardy television program: the answer is given within the text, and you must discover the question. Begin with the parallel statements you can see in the passage, list them, and only then ask, "What single subject ties these together? What question are these statements answering?" An example may be taken from John 1:1 and 14.

Njia nyingine ya kuunda muhtasari ni kupitia uinduktivu. Uinduktivu ni aina ya kufikiri inayoanza na mambo mahususi na kuelekea kwenye jambo la jumla (kutoka mifano hadi kanuni) — njia iliyo kinyume na udeduktivu. Inawezekana kuitazama milima, nyota, na bahari, kisha kuhitimisha kwamba lazima kuna Mungu wa ajabu aliyeviumba. Mtu anaangalia mifano mahususi na kufikia hitimisho la jumla. Katika kuhubiri, unaanza na hoja zinazopatikana katika kifungu na kurudi nyuma ili kuunda somo. Njia hii hutumika kutayarisha mahubiri ya kifungu na pia mahubiri ya kifafanuzi. Mchakato huu unafanana na kipindi cha televisheni cha mashindano kiitwacho Jeopardy: jibu limetolewa ndani ya kifungu, nawe lazima ugundue swali. Anza na kauli zinazolingana unazoziona katika kifungu, uziorodheshe, na hapo tu ndipo uulize, "Ni somo gani moja linalozifunga hizi pamoja? Kauli hizi zinajibu swali gani?" 4.3 E. Textual Sermon
4.3 E. Mahubiri ya Kifungu

When the main divisions of a sermon come from the text, as in the examples above, the sermon is called a textual sermon. The points come from the text, but the explanation of a textual sermon comes from the preacher. This is the simplest form of induction in preaching, and often the points are found in a single verse or two. Usually with a textual sermon, there is not enough information within the text to explain the point completely. In this case the preacher will explain the point from his general Biblical understanding. The text supplies the skeleton; the preacher supplies the flesh.

Migawanyo mikuu ya mahubiri inapotoka katika kifungu, kama katika mifano iliyo hapo juu, mahubiri hayo huitwa mahubiri ya kifungu. Hoja zinatoka katika kifungu, lakini maelezo ya mahubiri ya kifungu yanatoka kwa mhubiri. Hii ndiyo namna rahisi kabisa ya uinduktivu katika kuhubiri, na mara nyingi hoja hupatikana katika mstari mmoja au miwili. Kwa kawaida katika mahubiri ya kifungu, hakuna habari ya kutosha ndani ya kifungu kuieleza hoja kikamilifu. Katika hali hii mhubiri ataieleza hoja kutokana na ufahamu wake wa jumla wa Biblia. 4.4 F. Expository Sermon
4.4 F. Mahubiri ya Kifafanuzi

In the expository sermon, both the divisions and the explanations for them come from the text. Whereas only the divisions come from the text with a textual sermon, both the divisions and the subdivisions usually come from the text with an expository sermon. An expository sermon often makes use of more verses than a textual sermon. The greatest difference, however, is the treatment. An expository sermon seeks to explain the meaning of the passage studied more fully than the textual sermon. Structurally the expository sermon is most related to the text. The preacher is the messenger; the text is the message.

Katika mahubiri ya kifafanuzi, migawanyo pamoja na maelezo yake yote yanatoka katika kifungu. Wakati katika mahubiri ya kifungu ni migawanyo tu inayotoka katika kifungu, katika mahubiri ya kifafanuzi migawanyo na migawanyo midogo kwa kawaida vyote hutoka katika kifungu. Mahubiri ya kifafanuzi mara nyingi hutumia mistari mingi zaidi kuliko mahubiri ya kifungu. Hata hivyo, tofauti kubwa zaidi ni jinsi kifungu kinavyoshughulikiwa. Mahubiri ya kifafanuzi yanalenga kueleza maana ya kifungu kinachojifunzwa kwa ukamilifu zaidi kuliko mahubiri ya kifungu. Kimuundo, mahubiri ya kifafanuzi ndiyo yanayohusiana zaidi na kifungu. Mhubiri ni mjumbe; kifungu ndicho ujumbe.
