4.5 Putting Induction, Textual, and Expository Together
4.5 Kuunganisha Uinduktivu, Mahubiri ya Kifungu, na ya Kifafanuzi

Induction is the reasoning style: start with specifics in the text, conclude to a general subject. The textual sermon is the simplest application: divisions come from the text, but the preacher supplies the explanation from broader Biblical knowledge. The expository sermon is the fullest application: divisions and subdivisions both come from the text, and the explanation closely tracks the passage. All three sit on the same foundation — the conviction that the text drives the sermon, not the other way around. Topical preaching reasons from a subject down to texts; inductive preaching reasons from texts up to a subject. Both are legitimate, but inductive preaching gives the Bible the first word and the last word in the message.

Uinduktivu ni mtindo wa kufikiri: anza na mambo mahususi katika kifungu, kisha hitimisha kwa somo la jumla. Mahubiri ya kifungu ndiyo matumizi rahisi zaidi ya njia hii: migawanyo inatoka katika kifungu, lakini mhubiri anatoa maelezo kutokana na ujuzi wake mpana wa Biblia. Mahubiri ya kifafanuzi ndiyo matumizi kamili zaidi: migawanyo na migawanyo midogo vyote vinatoka katika kifungu, na maelezo yanafuata kifungu kwa karibu. Yote matatu yanasimama juu ya msingi uleule — imani thabiti kwamba kifungu ndicho kinachoongoza mahubiri, wala si kinyume chake. Mahubiri ya kimada hufikiri kutoka somo kushuka hadi vifungu; mahubiri ya kiinduktivu hufikiri kutoka vifungu kupanda hadi somo. Yote mawili ni halali, lakini mahubiri ya kiinduktivu huipa Biblia neno la kwanza na neno la mwisho katika ujumbe.

5.1 The EAI Method
5.1 Mbinu ya EAI

One of the simplest ways of developing the sermon after completing the outline is to use explanation, application, and illustration for each division. For purposes of this course we will call this the EAI Method. The order of these three elements may vary — you may start with illustration, proceed with application, and conclude with explanation. The same procedure is used for every point until the sermon is finished. Each of the three parts would normally receive the same attention, although they may not be exactly the same length. Repeat the procedure for topical, textual, or expository messages.

Mojawapo ya njia rahisi kabisa za kukuza mahubiri baada ya kukamilisha muhtasari ni kutumia ufafanuzi, matumizi, na kielelezo kwa kila mgawanyo. Kwa makusudi ya kozi hii tutaiita Mbinu ya EAI (kutoka herufi za kwanza za maneno ya Kiingereza Explanation, Application, Illustration). Mpangilio wa vipengele hivi vitatu unaweza kubadilika — unaweza kuanza na kielelezo, kuendelea na matumizi, na kumalizia na ufafanuzi. Utaratibu uleule hutumika kwa kila hoja mpaka mahubiri yakamilike. Kwa kawaida kila kimoja cha sehemu hizo tatu kingepewa uzito uleule, ingawa huenda visiwe na urefu sawa kabisa. Rudia utaratibu huu kwa mahubiri ya kimada, ya kifungu, au ya ufafanuzi wa Maandiko.
5.2 Explanation
5.2 Ufafanuzi

Explanation means "to bring out the meaning, to make plain, to make clear." This may take several different forms. (1) Explaining the meaning of the text — the interpreter asks, "What exactly was the Biblical writer saying to his hearers?" Here one seeks to draw out and explain the meaning of the text. (2) Narration — one gives the bare account of an event. You might tell the story of a Biblical character such as Daniel or Abraham. (3) Description — you describe how something appears to the five senses. You are painting a picture with words.

Ufafanuzi maana yake ni "kutoa maana, kuweka jambo wazi, kulifanya dhahiri." Huu unaweza kuchukua sura kadhaa tofauti. (1) Kufafanua maana ya kifungu — mfasiri anauliza, "Mwandishi wa Biblia alikuwa akiwaambia wasikilizaji wake nini hasa?" Hapa mtu anatafuta kutoa na kufafanua maana ya kifungu. (2) Usimulizi — mtu anatoa habari tupu ya tukio. Unaweza kusimulia hadithi ya mhusika wa Biblia kama vile Danieli au Ibrahimu. (3) Uelezaji — unaeleza jinsi kitu kinavyoonekana kwa milango mitano ya fahamu. Unachora picha kwa maneno.
5.3 Application — Master of All
5.3 Matumizi — Bwana wa Wote

Application is the master of all whereas the illustration is the servant of all. Charles H. Spurgeon said that application is where the sermon actually begins. It seeks to relate Biblical truth to people's lives. Otherwise it is just an historical Bible study. While there may be some value in such a study, it will not have much of an impact upon people's lives. Harry Emerson Fosdick said that people are not interested in what God said to the Jebusites. They are interested in what God is saying to them today through the story of the Jebusites.

Matumizi ni bwana wa wote, ilhali kielelezo ni mtumishi wa wote. Charles H. Spurgeon alisema kwamba matumizi ndipo mahubiri yanapoanza kwa kweli. Matumizi hutafuta kuunganisha kweli ya Biblia na maisha ya watu. La sivyo ni funzo la kihistoria la Biblia tu. Ingawa funzo la namna hiyo linaweza kuwa na faida fulani, halitakuwa na matokeo makubwa katika maisha ya watu. Harry Emerson Fosdick alisema kwamba watu hawapendezwi na kile Mungu alichowaambia Wayebusi. Wanapendezwa na kile Mungu anachowaambia wao leo kupitia habari ya Wayebusi.

Research suggests that unless the application is made by the speaker, it will not be made by the hearers. Application should be very personal — use "we" in speaking and answer "What should we do?" It should be in the present tense and should answer "What should we do right now?" It should be dynamic and changing — the truths of Scripture do not change, but applications of these truths do change with the times. It should suggest ways and means — "How are we to put this into practice today?"

Utafiti unaonyesha kwamba matumizi yasipofanywa na mnenaji, hayatafanywa na wasikilizaji. Matumizi yanapaswa kuwa ya binafsi sana — tumia "sisi" unaposema na ujibu swali, "Tufanye nini?" Yanapaswa kuwa katika wakati uliopo na kujibu swali, "Tufanye nini sasa hivi?" Yanapaswa kuwa hai na yenye kubadilika — kweli za Maandiko hazibadiliki, lakini matumizi ya kweli hizo hubadilika kadiri nyakati zinavyobadilika. Yanapaswa kupendekeza njia na mbinu — "Tutaliwekaje jambo hili katika vitendo leo?"
Show model: Then / Universal / Now method
Onyesha mfano: mbinu ya Wakati Ule / Kwa Wote / Sasa
Three steps to make an application:
Hatua tatu za kufanya matumizi:

(1) Then — what the text said to its original hearers. (2) Universal — the timeless principle that transcends culture. (3) Now — the specific application for today. Example: #1 Then. Jesus calmed the storm on the Sea of Galilee, and the storm in the lives of the disciples (Matthew 8:24-27). #2 Universal. Jesus has the power to calm outer and inner storms that rage in people's lives. #3 Now. Jesus calms outer and inner storms today such as loneliness, sickness, fear, and anxiety.

(1) Wakati Ule — kile kifungu kilichowaambia wasikilizaji wake wa kwanza.
(2) Kwa Wote — kanuni ya kudumu isiyofungwa na wakati, inayovuka mipaka ya utamaduni.
(3) Sasa — matumizi mahususi kwa ajili ya leo.

Mfano:
#1 Wakati Ule. Yesu alituliza dhoruba katika bahari ya Galilaya, na dhoruba katika maisha ya wanafunzi (Mathayo 8:24-27).
#2 Kwa Wote. Yesu ana uwezo wa kutuliza dhoruba za nje na za ndani zinazovuma katika maisha ya watu.
#3 Sasa. Yesu hutuliza dhoruba za nje na za ndani leo kama vile upweke, ugonjwa, hofu, na wasiwasi.
5.4 Illustration — Servant of All
5.4 Kielelezo — Mtumishi wa Wote

No book is completely adequate for producing illustrations. The word "illustrate" means to throw light upon. A human interest story makes the sermon come alive. Try for at least one good illustration per division — every point you make should be illustrated. I usually also use one in the introduction and one in the conclusion. Many students and pastors report that the finding of good illustrations is the most difficult task they face.

Hakuna kitabu kinachotosha kikamilifu kwa ajili ya kupata vielelezo. Neno "kuelezea kwa kielelezo" (illustrate) maana yake ni kutupa nuru juu ya jambo. Hadithi inayogusa maisha ya watu huyafanya mahubiri yawe hai. Jitahidi kuwa na angalau kielelezo kimoja kizuri kwa kila mgawanyo — kila hoja unayoitoa inapaswa kupewa kielelezo. Kwa kawaida mimi pia hutumia kimoja katika utangulizi na kimoja katika hitimisho. Wanafunzi na wachungaji wengi husema kwamba kupata vielelezo vizuri ndiyo kazi ngumu zaidi wanayokabiliana nayo.

Six sources of illustrations: (1) The Bible itself — biographies, parables, figures, or historical events. When you do this, the congregation may not know you are illustrating; you have the advantage of teaching the Bible at the same time. (2) Observation — keep a notebook of observations from nature, science, psychology, and people. Be discreet about using examples of church members or family. (3) Newspapers, newscasts, and news magazines — current events make Scripture feel immediate. (4) General reading and viewing — history, literature, films, novels. (5) Pastoral work — visits often produce illustrations; sometimes ask permission to share a story. (6) Personal experience — a form of testimony where you tell about something that happened to you.

Vyanzo sita vya vielelezo: (1) Biblia yenyewe — wasifu wa watu, mifano, tamathali, au matukio ya kihistoria. Unapofanya hivyo, huenda kusanyiko lisijue kwamba unatoa kielelezo; una faida ya kufundisha Biblia wakati huohuo. (2) Uchunguzi — weka daftari la mambo unayoyaona katika maumbile, sayansi, saikolojia, na watu. Kuwa na busara unapotumia mifano ya washiriki wa kanisa au ya familia. (3) Magazeti, taarifa za habari, na majarida ya habari — matukio ya sasa hufanya Maandiko yaonekane kuwa ya karibu na ya wakati huu. (4) Usomaji na utazamaji wa jumla — historia, fasihi, filamu, riwaya. (5) Kazi ya kichungaji — ziara mara nyingi huzaa vielelezo; wakati mwingine omba ruhusa kabla ya kusimulia habari fulani. (6) Uzoefu wa binafsi — aina ya ushuhuda ambamo unasimulia jambo lililokupata wewe mwenyewe.
5.5 Additional Subdivision Methodologies
5.5 Mbinu za Ziada za Kugawanya Hoja Ndogo

Apart from EAI there are several other methods for forming subpoints. With any of these the subpoints should appear in the preacher's notes but should very rarely be stated while delivering the sermon. Because preaching is an oral art form, too many subpoints are confusing rather than enlightening.

Mbali na EAI kuna mbinu nyingine kadhaa za kuunda hoja ndogo. Kwa mbinu yoyote kati ya hizi, hoja ndogo zinapaswa kuonekana katika maandishi ya mhubiri lakini mara chache sana zitajwe wakati wa kuhubiri. Kwa sababu kuhubiri ni sanaa ya mdomo, hoja ndogo nyingi mno huchanganya badala ya kuangaza.

1. The keyword method. A keyword is used in forming the subdivisions the same way a keyword links the main divisions. Each division could actually be a second sermon. Job 1:1 and Job 21:7 yield two great questions: "Why do the good suffer?" (subdivisions named with keyword positive results: Job learned of his pride, of patience, of God's providence) and "Why do the wicked prosper?" (subdivisions named with keyword reasons: things are not always as they appear; God's patience and mercy; one day God will make all things right).

1. Mbinu ya neno kiini. Neno kiini hutumika katika kuunda migawanyo midogo kwa namna ileile ambayo neno kiini huunganisha migawanyo mikuu. Kila mgawanyo unaweza kwa kweli kuwa mahubiri ya pili. Ayubu 1:1 na Ayubu 21:7 huzaa maswali mawili makubwa: "Kwa nini wema huteseka?" (migawanyo midogo iliyopewa jina kwa neno kiini matokeo mazuri: Ayubu alijifunza juu ya kiburi chake, juu ya uvumilivu, juu ya maongozi ya Mungu) na "Kwa nini waovu hufanikiwa?" (migawanyo midogo iliyopewa jina kwa neno kiini sababu: mambo si kila mara kama yanavyoonekana; uvumilivu na rehema za Mungu; siku moja Mungu atayanyoosha mambo yote).

2. The series of statements method. No attempt is made to discover a keyword for the subdivisions. The statements are rapid-fire concepts designed to provoke thought and stimulate word pictures. Mark 5:25-34, "He Touched Me" — Subject = Areas Jesus made the woman whole. Under "Christ made her physically whole" you might list: She had a foolish faith / She had an ignorant faith / She had a genuine faith. The healing was free; it was immediate.

2. Mbinu ya mfululizo wa kauli. Hakuna jitihada ya kutafuta neno kiini kwa ajili ya migawanyo midogo. Kauli hizo ni dhana zinazofuatana kwa haraka, zilizokusudiwa kuchochea fikira na kuamsha picha za maneno. Marko 5:25-34, "Alinigusa" — Somo = Maeneo ambamo Yesu alimfanya yule mwanamke kuwa mzima. Chini ya hoja "Kristo alimfanya kuwa mzima kimwili" unaweza kuorodhesha: Alikuwa na imani ya kipumbavu / Alikuwa na imani isiyo na ujuzi / Alikuwa na imani ya kweli. Uponyaji ulikuwa bure; ulikuwa wa papo hapo.

3. The combination method. Combine several methods, using one for one division and another for the next. The explanation method might be used for one point and the series of statements or keyword method for others.

3. Mbinu ya mchanganyiko. Changanya mbinu kadhaa, ukitumia moja kwa mgawanyo mmoja na nyingine kwa mgawanyo unaofuata. Mbinu ya ufafanuzi inaweza kutumika kwa hoja moja na mbinu ya mfululizo wa kauli au ya neno kiini kwa hoja nyingine.

4. EAI revisited. Return to EAI when the unit's content calls for substantial development on a single point — explanation drawn from the text, application drawn from the universal-to-now bridge, illustration drawn from any of the six sources above.

4. EAI kwa mara nyingine. Rudi kwenye EAI pale maudhui ya sehemu yanapohitaji ukuzaji wa kina juu ya hoja moja — ufafanuzi unaotokana na kifungu, matumizi yanayotokana na daraja la kutoka kanuni ya kudumu kwa wote hadi sasa, kielelezo kinachotokana na chanzo chochote kati ya vile sita vilivyotajwa hapo juu.

6.1 A Touch of Beauty
6.1 Mguso wa Uzuri

Outlines seem to be stronger, and are remembered more easily, when each point is five or fewer words in length. Another important ingredient of beauty is parallelism. With parallelism you try to extend the exact wording of each division for as long as possible. In most instances parallelism helps the hearers to remember the message, and it produces a nicer outline. This may or may not involve alliteration, the repetition of a sound.

Mihtasari huonekana kuwa na nguvu zaidi, na hukumbukwa kwa urahisi zaidi, pale kila hoja ina urefu wa maneno matano au machache zaidi. Kiungo kingine muhimu cha uzuri ni usambamba. Katika usambamba unajaribu kuendeleza maneno yaleyale hasa ya kila mgawanyo kwa muda mrefu kadiri iwezekanavyo. Mara nyingi usambamba huwasaidia wasikilizaji kukumbuka ujumbe, na huzaa muhtasari mzuri zaidi. Hii inaweza kuhusisha au isihusishe takriri ya sauti (alliteration), yaani kurudiwa kwa sauti moja.

A message is usually stronger if it is in the active voice instead of the passive voice. Voice is a grammatical term used to tell whether the subject of the sentence is acting or receiving the action expressed by the verb. "John the Baptist proclaimed the arrival of Christ" (active) is stronger than "The arrival of Christ was preached by John the Baptist" (passive). Sometimes you may begin with a rough outline in which two of the points are active and one is passive; it may be possible to change the voice of the passive point without changing the meaning. Sometimes the divisions may be reworded so that a nicer outline is developed while retaining the essential integrity of the text.

Ujumbe kwa kawaida huwa na nguvu zaidi ukiwa katika kauli tendaji badala ya kauli tendwa. Kauli ni istilahi ya kisarufi inayotumika kuonyesha kama kiima cha sentensi kinatenda au kinapokea tendo linaloelezwa na kitenzi. "Yohana Mbatizaji alitangaza kuja kwa Kristo" (kauli tendaji) ina nguvu zaidi kuliko "Kuja kwa Kristo kulihubiriwa na Yohana Mbatizaji" (kauli tendwa). Wakati mwingine unaweza kuanza na muhtasari wa awali ambamo hoja mbili ziko katika kauli tendaji na moja iko katika kauli tendwa; huenda ikawezekana kubadilisha kauli ya hoja iliyo tendwa bila kubadilisha maana. Wakati mwingine migawanyo inaweza kupangwa upya kwa maneno mengine ili muhtasari mzuri zaidi ukuzwe huku uadilifu wa msingi wa kifungu ukidumishwa.

6.2 The Beauty of Simplicity
6.2 Uzuri wa Urahisi

For us to use words like justification, spiritual, faith, repentance, righteous, calling, fellowship, conversion, holiness, ordain, sanctification, glorification, propitiation, or redemption is often to miss the mark. Most people in the pew will not understand what we are talking about. Even simpler words like church, letter, faith, or grace will often not communicate. If we are trying to attract people with little or no church background, we must be understandable. It is important therefore to explain in simple terms what we want to say. Jesus managed to communicate important theological concepts with the use of parables.

Sisi kutumia maneno kama kuhesabiwa haki, -a kiroho, imani, toba, mwenye haki, wito, ushirika, kuongoka, utakatifu, kuweka wakfu, utakaso, kutukuzwa, kipatanisho, au ukombozi mara nyingi ni kukosa shabaha. Watu wengi walioketi kanisani hawataelewa tunachozungumzia. Hata maneno rahisi zaidi kama kanisa, waraka, imani, au neema mara nyingi hayatawasilisha ujumbe. Ikiwa tunajaribu kuwavuta watu wenye historia ndogo au wasio na historia yoyote ya kanisa, lazima tueleweke. Kwa hiyo ni muhimu kueleza kwa maneno rahisi kile tunachotaka kusema. Yesu aliweza kuwasilisha dhana muhimu za kitheolojia kwa kutumia mifano.
6.3 The Finishing Touches — Title, Transition, Introduction
6.3 Miguso ya Mwisho — Kichwa, Kiunganishi, Utangulizi
A sermon is composed of three primary parts: the introduction, the body, and the conclusion. We have been working primarily on the body up to this point. Now we will insert the finishing touches.
Hotuba ya mahubiri ina sehemu kuu tatu: utangulizi, kiini, na hitimisho. Mpaka sasa tumekuwa tukifanya kazi hasa juu ya kiini. Sasa tutaweka miguso ya mwisho.

Title. The title is the name you give to the sermon — what it is called. The primary purpose for having a title is for advertising the sermon. You are trying to catch the listener's attention. Some pastors post the sermon title on the church sign; others place the title in the bulletin. The title may sometimes be the same as the subject, but this is not always true. Many effective titles relate to human needs: "How to Raise Your Kids," "How to Have a Happy Home," "How to Cope with Stress," "How to Manage Your Money."

Kichwa. Kichwa ni jina unalolipa mahubiri — yanavyoitwa. Kusudi kuu la kuwa na kichwa ni kuyatangaza mahubiri. Unajaribu kuvuta usikivu wa msikilizaji. Wachungaji wengine huweka kichwa cha mahubiri kwenye ubao wa matangazo wa kanisa; wengine huweka kichwa katika taarifa ya ibada. Wakati mwingine kichwa kinaweza kuwa sawa na somo, lakini si hivyo kila mara. Vichwa vingi vinavyofaa huhusiana na mahitaji ya wanadamu: "Jinsi ya Kulea Watoto Wako," "Jinsi ya Kuwa na Nyumba yenye Furaha," "Jinsi ya Kukabiliana na Msongo wa Mawazo," "Jinsi ya Kusimamia Fedha Zako."

Transition. The transition is a moving from one section of the sermon to another. You need a transition from the introduction into the body, between the divisions, and in moving from the divisions to the conclusion. The major transition is going from the introduction to the body. This transition should include the subject and may be stated, "Let us examine (transition) some answers as to who Christ is (statement of the subject)."

Kiunganishi. Kiunganishi ni kuhama kutoka sehemu moja ya mahubiri hadi nyingine. Unahitaji kiunganishi kutoka utangulizi kuingia kiini, kati ya migawanyo, na unapohama kutoka migawanyo kwenda hitimisho. Kiunganishi kikuu ni kile cha kutoka utangulizi kwenda kiini. Kiunganishi hiki kinapaswa kujumuisha somo na kinaweza kutamkwa hivi: "Hebu tuchunguze (kiunganishi) baadhi ya majibu kuhusu Kristo ni nani (kauli ya somo)."

Introduction. An introduction leads into the sermon and should comprise five to twenty percent of a sermon. The introduction seeks to gain attention, to let the people know why the sermon is important, to give the purpose of the sermon, and to establish rapport with the audience. I nearly always prepare the introduction after completing everything else. I like to know what I am introducing before putting it down. Two primary types: textual introduction (discusses geography, history, archaeology, setting and customs surrounding the text) and subject introduction (introduces the topic itself in a unique and interesting way — often by free association from a personal memory or current event).

Utangulizi. Utangulizi huongoza kuingia katika mahubiri na unapaswa kuchukua asilimia tano hadi ishirini ya mahubiri. Utangulizi hutafuta kuvuta usikivu, kuwajulisha watu kwa nini mahubiri ni muhimu, kutoa kusudi la mahubiri, na kujenga ukaribu na wasikilizaji. Karibu kila mara mimi huandaa utangulizi baada ya kukamilisha kila kitu kingine. Napenda kujua ninachokitambulisha kabla ya kukiandika. Aina kuu mbili: utangulizi wa kifungu (unazungumzia jiografia, historia, akiolojia, mazingira na desturi zinazokizunguka kifungu) na utangulizi wa somo (unaitambulisha mada yenyewe kwa namna ya kipekee na ya kuvutia — mara nyingi kwa kuhusisha mawazo kwa uhuru kutoka katika kumbukumbu ya binafsi au tukio la sasa).
6.4 The Conclusion
6.4 Hitimisho

The conclusion leads out of the sermon. It should include the objective — a practical way to implement what you have said. The conclusion is not a place to introduce new material. You may restate your major ideas or draw conclusions from the points. I usually go directly from the final division into the invitation without a sharp break. Four methods:

Hitimisho huongoza kutoka nje ya mahubiri. Linapaswa kujumuisha lengo — njia ya kivitendo ya kutekeleza ulichosema. Hitimisho si mahali pa kuleta mambo mapya. Unaweza kurudia mawazo yako makuu au kutoa mahitimisho kutokana na hoja. Kwa kawaida mimi huenda moja kwa moja kutoka mgawanyo wa mwisho kuingia katika mwaliko bila kukatiza ghafla. Mbinu nne:

1. The Illustration or Story Conclusion. A powerful, moving illustration right before the final appeal softens hearts and allows the Holy Spirit to speak without restraint. Roy Fish recounts Robert Ingersoll, the noted infidel, repeatedly daring his audiences to stand if any still claimed Christ — until two teenage girls rose in a midwestern theater and walked the aisle singing "Stand Up, Stand Up for Jesus," joined by almost the entire audience. 2. The Summary Conclusion. A restatement and recapitulation of the main ideas. New ideas should not be introduced. One exception: an appeal drawn directly from the text — Jesus' "Go and do likewise" at the end of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:37, NKJV). 3. The Inference Conclusion. After stating the main ideas, draw out inferences from them. From a subject "reasons for believing in the Resurrection" — empty tomb, disciples' boldness, verified appearances — infer: "Therefore we may conclude that we serve a Lord who is alive today." 4. The Prayer Conclusion. Some pastors make an appeal and then conclude with a prayer before the invitation. Effective when done well, but runs the risk of breaking the continuity of the appeal.

1. Hitimisho la Kielelezo au Hadithi. Kielelezo chenye nguvu na kinachogusa moyo kikitolewa kabla tu ya wito wa mwisho hulainisha mioyo na kumruhusu Roho Mtakatifu kunena bila kizuizi. Roy Fish anasimulia habari ya Robert Ingersoll, kafiri mashuhuri, aliyewapa wasikilizaji wake changamoto mara kwa mara wasimame ikiwa yupo yeyote ambaye bado alidai kuwa wa Kristo — mpaka wasichana wawili wa umri wa ujana waliposimama katika jumba la maonyesho huko magharibi ya kati ya Marekani na kutembea katika njia ya katikati wakiimba "Simameni, Simameni kwa Yesu" ("Stand Up, Stand Up for Jesus"), wakaungwa mkono na karibu wasikilizaji wote.
2. Hitimisho la Muhtasari wa Mawazo. Kurudia na kufupisha upya mawazo makuu. Mawazo mapya hayapaswi kuletwa. Upekee mmoja: wito unaotokana moja kwa moja na kifungu — maneno ya Yesu "Enenda zako, nawe ukafanye vivyo hivyo" mwishoni mwa habari ya Msamaria mwema (Luka 10:37, NKJV).
3. Hitimisho la Kimantiki. Baada ya kutaja mawazo makuu, toa makisio ya kimantiki kutokana nayo. Kutoka kwa somo "sababu za kuamini Ufufuo" — kaburi tupu, ujasiri wa wanafunzi, kuonekana kwake kulikothibitishwa — kisia kimantiki: "Kwa hiyo tunaweza kuhitimisha kwamba tunamtumikia Bwana aliye hai leo."
4. Hitimisho la Maombi. Wachungaji wengine hutoa wito kisha humalizia kwa maombi kabla ya mwaliko. Linafaa likifanywa vizuri, lakini lina hatari ya kuvunja mwendelezo wa wito.
6.5 The Preaching Analysis
6.5 Uchambuzi wa Kuhubiri

Now that you understand the mechanics of constructing a sermon, here is one final tool: the preaching analysis. This tool will help you examine the Bible book by book and find sermonic subjects. If you do a preaching analysis of the books of the Bible, you will have enough possible sermon topics and outlines to last your complete ministry — though such an analysis of the whole Bible could very well take most of your years of ministry.

Sasa kwa kuwa unaelewa ufundi wa kujenga hotuba ya mahubiri, hiki hapa ni chombo kimoja cha mwisho: uchambuzi wa kuhubiri. Chombo hiki kitakusaidia kuichunguza Biblia kitabu kwa kitabu na kupata masomo ya kuhubiri. Ukifanya uchambuzi wa kuhubiri wa vitabu vya Biblia, utakuwa na mada na mihtasari ya mahubiri inayowezekana ya kutosha kudumu katika huduma yako yote — ingawa uchambuzi wa namna hiyo wa Biblia nzima unaweza kabisa kuchukua miaka mingi ya huduma yako.

A preaching analysis involves going through the text and using induction to find the probing question and an outline. It is much different from a chapter or passage outline; it begins with the discovery of common concepts within the text. The concepts may cover from one to several verses. After identifying these concepts, you use an inductive approach to discover the probing question. Often the probing question will contain the subject of the passage. Sometimes there will be a probing question within a larger probing question. Beside the probing question and concepts, you may want to write the verses. After completing the analysis, you may go back and begin to form outlines. Not all the analysis outlines are suitable for preaching outlines, but they can help in formulating them. Many pastors find an analysis especially helpful when preaching consecutive sermons through a book.

Uchambuzi wa kuhubiri unahusisha kupitia kifungu na kutumia njia ya kiinduktivi (kuanzia mambo mahususi hadi kanuni ya jumla) ili kupata swali la uchunguzi na muhtasari. Ni tofauti sana na muhtasari wa sura au wa kifungu; unaanza na kugundua dhana za pamoja ndani ya kifungu. Dhana hizo zinaweza kuhusu kuanzia mstari mmoja hadi mistari kadhaa. Baada ya kutambua dhana hizi, unatumia njia ya kiinduktivi kugundua swali la uchunguzi. Mara nyingi swali la uchunguzi litakuwa na somo la kifungu. Wakati mwingine kutakuwa na swali la uchunguzi ndani ya swali kubwa zaidi la uchunguzi. Kando ya swali la uchunguzi na dhana, unaweza kutaka kuandika mistari. Baada ya kukamilisha uchambuzi, unaweza kurudi nyuma na kuanza kuunda mihtasari. Si mihtasari yote ya uchambuzi inayofaa kuwa mihtasari ya kuhubiri, lakini inaweza kusaidia katika kuiunda. Wachungaji wengi huona uchambuzi kuwa wa msaada hasa wanapohubiri mfululizo wa mahubiri kupitia kitabu kimoja.

Preaching from the Inside Out
Kuhubiri Kutoka Ndani Kwenda Nje
Thorough study and a full manuscript, then internalization, a simple keyword note, and natural delivery. The method is not "prepare less." It is to prepare until the sermon belongs to the preacher.

Kujifunza kwa kina na kuandika mswada kamili, kisha kuyaweka mahubiri moyoni, kikaratasi rahisi cha maneno kiini, na uwasilishaji wa kawaida usio wa kulazimisha. Mbinu hii si "jiandae kidogo." Ni kujiandaa mpaka mahubiri yawe mali ya mhubiri mwenyewe.
7.1 The Purpose of This Unit
7.1 Kusudi la Sehemu Hii

Inaunganisha kazi ya kujenga mahubiri, ambayo sehemu zilizotangulia zilifundisha, na kazi ya kuyawasilisha, ambayo sehemu inayofuata itaishughulikia.

7.2 Case Study: Galatians 4:4 — God's Perfect Plan
7.2 Mfano Halisi: Wagalatia 4:4 — Mpango Kamili wa Mungu
"But when the fulness of the time came, God sent forth his Son, born of a woman, born under the law."Galatians 4:4 (ASV)
"Hata ulipowadia utimilifu wa wakati, Mungu alimtuma Mwanawe, amezaliwa na mwanamke, amezaliwa chini ya sheria."<cite>Wagalatia 4:4 (SUV)</cite>

The surviving materials preserve different stages of one sermon's development. The handwritten Galatians 4:4 note below is an earlier retrieval form. The surviving Word manuscript, reproduced later in this unit, developed the same material into a First Advent / Second Advent structure. They are related materials, not an exact note-and-manuscript pair from the same revision, so do not read the note as a copy of that final manuscript.

Nyaraka zilizohifadhiwa zinaonyesha hatua tofauti za ukuaji wa mahubiri yale yale. Kikaratasi kilichoandikwa kwa mkono cha Wagalatia 4:4 kilicho hapa chini ni muundo wa awali wa kukumbusha. Mswada wa Word uliohifadhiwa, unaonakiliwa baadaye katika sehemu hii, uliendeleza habari zile zile kuwa muundo wa Ujio wa Kwanza / Ujio wa Pili. Hizi ni nyaraka zinazohusiana, si jozi kamili ya kikaratasi na mswada kutoka toleo lile lile la marekebisho; kwa hiyo usikisome kikaratasi kana kwamba ni nakala ya mswada huo wa mwisho.

The manuscript develops Jewish morality, Alexander and Greek culture and language, the Septuagint, Roman peace, roads, safety, and postal communication at length. The small note reduces those large blocks of prepared thought to a handful of cues.

Mswada unaeleza kwa urefu maadili ya Kiyahudi, Aleksanda na utamaduni na lugha ya Kigiriki, Septuajinti, amani ya Kirumi, barabara, usalama, na mawasiliano ya posta. Kikaratasi kidogo kinapunguza sehemu hizo kubwa za mawazo yaliyoandaliwa kuwa vidokezo vichache tu.
The actual handwritten pulpit note Wayne Cook used to preach Galatians 4:4 (English original).
Kikaratasi halisi cha mimbarini kilichoandikwa kwa mkono ambacho Wayne Cook alikitumia kuhubiri Wagalatia 4:4 (asili kwa Kiingereza).
7.3 The Simplicity of the Keyword Model
7.3 Urahisi wa Mtindo wa Maneno ya Ufunguo

A keyword is not a miniature sermon. It is a personal retrieval signal. "Alexander / Aristotle" can reopen a developed historical discussion. A story label such as "Brooklyn Bridge" can retrieve an entire narrative. The note functions as an index into prepared material already stored in the mind.

Neno kiini si mahubiri madogo. Ni ishara binafsi ya kukumbusha. "Aleksanda / Aristotle" linaweza kufungua tena maelezo kamili ya kihistoria yaliyoandaliwa. Jina la hadithi kama "Daraja la Brooklyn" linaweza kurejesha simulizi nzima. Kikaratasi kinafanya kazi kama orodha-elekezi ya habari zilizoandaliwa ambazo tayari zimehifadhiwa akilini.

Working ModelPoint → Explain → Apply → Illustrate. The point tells the preacher where he is; explanatory and biblical cues restore the chain of thought; application identifies what the truth asks of the hearer; illustration becomes a memorable landmark. The preacher knows what to think about next without memorizing exactly how he will say it.

Mtindo wa Kufanyia Kazi
Hoja → Eleza → Tumia → Toa kielelezo. Hoja inamwonyesha mhubiri mahali alipo; vidokezo vya maelezo na vya Biblia vinarejesha mtiririko wa mawazo; matumizi yanaonyesha kile ambacho kweli hiyo inamtaka msikilizaji afanye; kielelezo kinakuwa alama ya njia isiyosahaulika. Mhubiri anajua atafikiri nini baadaye bila kukariri jinsi hasa atakavyolisema.
7.4 Stories as Memory Anchors
7.4 Hadithi kama Nanga za Kumbukumbu

Stories are unusually efficient retrieval units because they contain sequence, people, setting, tension, and outcome. A short cue can "decompress" into substantial material. The same quality helps the congregation: a remembered story can retrieve the truth attached to it.

Hadithi ni vitengo vya kukumbuka vyenye ufanisi wa ajabu kwa sababu zina mfuatano, watu, mazingira, mvutano, na matokeo. Kidokezo kifupi kinaweza "kufunguka" na kutoa habari nyingi. Sifa hiyo hiyo inawasaidia washiriki pia: hadithi inayokumbukwa inaweza kurejesha kweli iliyoambatanishwa nayo.

Older homiletical cautions rightly warn against allowing an illustration to eclipse biblical truth. Yet Jesus often taught through parables in which the story did more than decorate a proposition: the story carried or disclosed the truth. The test is whether the story serves the text and advances understanding and application.

Tahadhari za zamani za elimu ya uhubiri zinaonya kwa haki dhidi ya kuruhusu kielelezo kufunika kweli ya Biblia. Hata hivyo Yesu mara nyingi alifundisha kwa mifano ambamo hadithi ilifanya zaidi ya kupamba kauli: hadithi yenyewe ilibeba au kufunua kweli. Kipimo ni kama hadithi inakitumikia kifungu na kuendeleza uelewa na matumizi.
7.5 Internalization, Not Memorization
7.5 Kuweka Moyoni, Si Kukariri

The goal is not sentence memorization. The preacher internalizes the sermon's location and direction: where each major idea belongs and how the ideas connect. Strong structure creates freedom. If wording changes, an illustration moves, or a thought is expanded or shortened, the preacher still knows where the sermon is going.

Lengo si kukariri sentensi. Mhubiri anayaweka moyoni mahali na mwelekeo wa mahubiri: kila wazo kubwa linakaa wapi na mawazo yanaunganikaje. Muundo imara huleta uhuru. Maneno yakibadilika, kielelezo kikihamishwa, au wazo likipanuliwa au kufupishwa, mhubiri bado anajua mahubiri yanaelekea wapi.
The manuscript is where the preacher develops the sermon. The pulpit note is where the preacher retrieves it.
Mswada ndipo mhubiri anapoyaandaa mahubiri. Kikaratasi cha mimbarini ndipo mhubiri anapoyarejesha.
The Forgotten-Bible Test
Kipimo cha Biblia Iliyosahaulika

On one occasion I arrived without my Bible. I borrowed a Bible from the church library, wrote my outline on a borrowed Post-it note, and preached. Members said it was the same as usual. The lesson is not that a preacher needs neither Bible nor preparation. The opposite is true: the sermon had been prepared and internalized so thoroughly that recreating the retrieval map was sufficient to guide delivery.

Siku moja nilifika bila Biblia yangu. Niliazima Biblia kutoka maktaba ya kanisa, nikaandika muhtasari wangu kwenye kikaratasi cha kunata (Post-it) nilichoazima, nikahubiri. Washiriki walisema ilikuwa kama kawaida. Funzo si kwamba mhubiri hahitaji Biblia wala maandalizi. Kinyume chake ndicho kweli: mahubiri yalikuwa yameandaliwa na kuwekwa moyoni kwa kina kiasi kwamba kuchora upya ramani ya kukumbuka kulitosha kuongoza uwasilishaji.

Kinachofuata kimenakiliwa kutoka faili la Word la Wagalatia 4:4 lililohifadhiwa, badala ya kuandikwa upya kwa ajili ya sehemu hii. Maelezo yaliyo pembeni yanaonyesha sifa za mswada zilizo muhimu kwa mbinu ya kuhubiri. Faili linamalizika kwa muhtasari mfupi wa mhubiri mwenyewe wa mahubiri yale yale, unaoonyeshwa baada ya mswada.

Title: God's Perfect Plan
Kichwa: Mpango Kamili wa Mungu

Introduction. The movie Arrival, released a few years ago, depicts several mysterious alien spacecraft suddenly appearing around the globe. Dr. Louise Banks, a brilliant linguist, is tasked with understanding a mysterious alien language. As she delves into this language, she discovers a strange truth about time. It is not just a straight linear line.

Utangulizi. Filamu Arrival ("Kuwasili"), iliyotolewa miaka michache iliyopita, inaonyesha vyombo kadhaa vya angani vya kigeni vyenye fumbo vikitokea ghafla sehemu mbalimbali za dunia. Dkt. Louise Banks, mtaalamu hodari wa lugha, anapewa jukumu la kuelewa lugha ya ajabu ya viumbe hao wa kigeni. Anapozama katika lugha hiyo, anagundua kweli ya ajabu kuhusu wakati. Wakati si mstari mmoja ulionyooka tu.

Our text talks about God's time, the perfect time ...the arrival of our Lord Jesus during an advent. The word "advent" means "a coming" or "arrival." During this season, we learn of God's perfect plan with the coming of our Savior into the world. So Galatians 4:4 states, "But when the fullness of time had come, God sent forth his Son, born of woman, born under the law."

Kifungu chetu kinazungumzia wakati wa Mungu, wakati mkamilifu... kuwasili kwa Bwana wetu Yesu katika ujio. Neno "ujio" (advent) maana yake ni "kuja" au "kuwasili." Katika msimu huu, tunajifunza juu ya mpango kamili wa Mungu kwa kuja kwa Mwokozi wetu ulimwenguni. Kwa hiyo Wagalatia 4:4 inasema, "Hata ulipowadia utimilifu wa wakati, Mungu alimtuma Mwanawe, amezaliwa na mwanamke, amezaliwa chini ya sheria."
I want to look today at not one, but the dual Advents of Jesus.
Leo nataka kutazama si ujio mmoja tu, bali ujio wa Yesu wa mara mbili.

I. The First Advent. Jesus’ arrival in Bethlehem. "Well, it's about time!" is an expression we use when someone is late and we are frustrated. Surely people wondered why God did not send the Messiah when expected. 400 years had elapsed since there had even been a prophet in Israel. God seemed distant and silent. But in looking back we can see how God had carefully prepared for this arrival.

I. Ujio wa Kwanza. Kuwasili kwa Yesu huko Bethlehemu. "Afadhali, hatimaye umefika!" ni usemi tunaoutumia mtu anapochelewa nasi tumekasirika. Bila shaka watu walijiuliza kwa nini Mungu hakumtuma Masihi wakati walipomtarajia. Miaka 400 ilikuwa imepita tangu kuwe hata na nabii mmoja katika Israeli. Mungu alionekana kuwa mbali na kunyamaza. Lakini tukitazama nyuma tunaweza kuona jinsi Mungu alivyokuwa ameandaa kwa uangalifu kuwasili huku.
A. Prophecies of the birth. There were over 300 prophecies in the Old Testament about the Messiah. Today we're going to look at two related to Jesus' birth.
A. Unabii kuhusu kuzaliwa. Kulikuwa na unabii zaidi ya 300 katika Agano la Kale kuhusu Masihi. Leo tutatazama miwili inayohusiana na kuzaliwa kwa Yesu.
Isaiah 7:14: The Virgin Birth. "A virgin shall have a son, and shall call his name Emmanuel, which means God with us."
Isaya 7:14: Kuzaliwa na Bikira. "Bikira atazaa mwana, naye atamwita jina lake Imanueli, maana yake, Mungu pamoja nasi."

During the time of Isaiah, the Kingdom of Judah, the southern Kingdom of Israel, was under threat from the powerful Assyrian Empire. Because Ahaz's enemies were forming an alliance, Ahaz decided to get his own partner -- Egypt. Isaiah went up to the king and told him to trust in the Lord and not in a scheming alliance with Egypt. But Ahaz is unfaithful and doubts that God is really going to come through for him. So Isaiah said, "Ask the Lord for a sign." Ahaz hypocritically says, "I don't want to insult God by asking for a sign.' Isaiah said, "Well God will give you a sign anyway. A virgin shall have a son, and shall call his name Emmanuel, which means God with us."

Wakati wa Isaya, Ufalme wa Yuda, ufalme wa kusini wa Israeli, ulikuwa chini ya tishio la Dola yenye nguvu ya Ashuru. Kwa kuwa adui za Ahazi walikuwa wakiunda muungano, Ahazi aliamua kujitafutia mshirika wake mwenyewe -- Misri. Isaya alimwendea mfalme akamwambia amtumaini Bwana na si muungano wa hila na Misri. Lakini Ahazi si mwaminifu, naye anatilia shaka kwamba kweli Mungu atamtendea kama alivyoahidi. Kwa hiyo Isaya akasema, "Mwombe Bwana ishara." Ahazi kwa unafiki anasema, "Sitaki kumkosea Mungu heshima kwa kuomba ishara." Isaya akasema, "Basi Mungu atakupa ishara hata hivyo. Bikira atazaa mwana, naye atamwita jina lake Imanueli, maana yake, Mungu pamoja nasi."

Isaiah prophesied that a young woman would conceive and bear a son, naming him Immanuel, which means "God with us." The immediate context of the prophecy was a sign of God's protection for Judah, so somehow, I believe God fulfilled the prophecy in that day. But an even more astounding New Testament prophecy was to come, ultimately pointing to the miraculous birth of the Messiah, Jesus the Christ.

Isaya alitabiri kwamba msichana angechukua mimba na kuzaa mwana, na kumwita Imanueli, maana yake "Mungu pamoja nasi." Muktadha wa karibu wa unabii huo ulikuwa ishara ya ulinzi wa Mungu kwa Yuda, kwa hiyo naamini kwamba kwa namna fulani Mungu aliutimiza unabii huo siku zile. Lakini utimilifu wa kushangaza zaidi ulikuwa bado unakuja katika Agano Jipya, ukielekeza hatimaye kwenye kuzaliwa kwa muujiza kwa Masihi, Yesu Kristo.

So this prophecy of the Virgin birth was given. Then 700 years slowly pass by. The great hour arrives, the clock of eternity runs out; it is time for the Savior to be born. Now we see God picking out a human mother to bring his son into the world. In Galilee he found a young woman named Mary who was engaged to Joseph to be the child's mother.

Basi unabii huu wa kuzaliwa na Bikira ulitolewa. Kisha miaka 700 inapita polepole. Saa kuu inafika, saa ya milele inatimia; ni wakati wa Mwokozi kuzaliwa. Sasa tunamwona Mungu akimchagua mama wa kibinadamu wa kumleta Mwanawe ulimwenguni. Huko Galilaya alimpata msichana jina lake Mariamu, aliyekuwa ameposwa na Yusufu, ili awe mama wa mtoto huyo.

Micah 5:2: The Birthplace of the Messiah. “But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come for me one who will be ruler over Israel." Micah prophesied during a time of political turmoil and division in Israel. His prophecies often focused on the hope of restoration and the coming of a righteous ruler.

Mika 5:2: Mahali pa Kuzaliwa Masihi. "Bali wewe, Bethlehemu Efrata, uliye mdogo miongoni mwa koo za Yuda, kutoka kwako atanitokea mmoja atakayekuwa mtawala katika Israeli." Mika alitabiri wakati wa machafuko ya kisiasa na mgawanyiko katika Israeli. Unabii wake mara nyingi ulikazia tumaini la kurejeshwa na kuja kwa mtawala mwenye haki.

Micah specifically identified Bethlehem as the birthplace of the coming Messiah. This small town, associated with King David's lineage, was an unlikely place for the birth of a great ruler. However, the prophecy points to the humble beginnings of Jesus, the long-awaited Messiah. The religious leaders under Herod rightly identified Bethlehem as the place of the child's birth. To remove the threat of a king, Herod killed all the infants in the area under 2 years of age. So first there are prophecies about the birth, preparing the nation for the coming of the Messiah. He would be born of a virgin and in Bethlehem.

Mika alitaja Bethlehemu waziwazi kuwa mahali atakapozaliwa Masihi ajaye. Mji huu mdogo, unaohusishwa na ukoo wa Mfalme Daudi, haukutarajiwa kuwa mahali pa kuzaliwa kwa mtawala mkuu. Hata hivyo unabii huo unaelekeza kwenye mwanzo wa unyenyekevu wa Yesu, Masihi aliyengojewa kwa muda mrefu. Viongozi wa dini chini ya Herode walitambua kwa usahihi kwamba Bethlehemu ndipo mahali mtoto angezaliwa. Ili kuondoa tishio la mfalme mwingine, Herode aliwaua watoto wachanga wote wa eneo lile wenye umri chini ya miaka 2. Kwa hiyo kwanza kuna unabii kuhusu kuzaliwa, ukilitayarisha taifa kwa kuja kwa Masihi. Angezaliwa na bikira, na huko Bethlehemu.
B. High Jewish Morality
B. Maadili ya Juu ya Kiyahudi

Religiously, the ancient world was sunk in a moral abyss so deep that even pagans cried out against it. Spiritual hunger was everywhere evident as witnessed by the prevalent appeal within every social stratum for spiritual insight from religions introduced from the east. The religions in apparent ascendancy within the empire were exactly those ancient religions which had once been confronted by the prophets of God when the Hebrew peoples first entered the Promised Land.

Kidini, ulimwengu wa kale ulikuwa umezama katika shimo la uovu wa kimaadili lenye kina kirefu sana hata wapagani wenyewe walililalamikia. Njaa ya kiroho ilionekana kila mahali, kama ilivyothibitishwa na kiu iliyoenea katika kila tabaka la jamii ya kutafuta ufahamu wa kiroho kutoka kwa dini zilizoletwa kutoka mashariki. Dini zilizoonekana kupata nguvu ndani ya dola zilikuwa hasa zile dini za kale ambazo manabii wa Mungu walikuwa wamepambana nazo zamani wakati Waebrania walipoingia kwanza katika Nchi ya Ahadi.

When many pagans saw the difference of Judaism....a high standard of morality they were attracted to it. They believed in one God and even worshipped in the Jewish synagogues. Cornelius was one of these. To actually become a Jew required circumcision of the men. For many that was a step too far. But they were called God-fearers because they feared God and wanted an association with the God of Israel.

Wapagani wengi walipoona tofauti ya dini ya Kiyahudi... kiwango cha juu cha maadili, walivutiwa nayo. Waliamini Mungu mmoja na hata waliabudu katika masinagogi ya Kiyahudi. Kornelio alikuwa mmoja wao. Ili mtu awe Myahudi kweli, wanaume walihitaji kutahiriwa. Kwa wengi hiyo ilikuwa hatua ya kupita kiasi. Lakini waliitwa wamchao Mungu kwa sababu walimcha Mungu na walitaka kuhusiana na Mungu wa Israeli.
C. Prominent Greek Language and Culture.
C. Lugha na Utamaduni wa Kigiriki Uliotawala.

Alexander the Great, who lived in the 4th century B.C., began the conquest of the civilized world, and took with him his teacher Aristotle. And Alexander the Great made the whole civilized world Hellenist, Greek. Greek institutions, Greek philosophy, Greek architecture, Greek culture and Greek language; from one side of the empire to the other, the whole civilized world became Greek. They spoke Greek.

Aleksanda Mkuu, aliyeishi katika karne ya 4 K.K., alianza kuushinda ulimwengu uliostaarabika, akamchukua pamoja naye mwalimu wake Aristotle. Na Aleksanda Mkuu aliufanya ulimwengu wote uliostaarabika kuwa wa Kiyunani (Kihelenisti), wa Kigiriki. Taasisi za Kigiriki, falsafa ya Kigiriki, usanifu wa majengo wa Kigiriki, utamaduni wa Kigiriki na lugha ya Kigiriki; kutoka upande mmoja wa dola hadi upande mwingine, ulimwengu wote uliostaarabika ukawa wa Kigiriki. Walizungumza Kigiriki.

When Alexander died at the age of thirty-three, he was the same age as our Lord. When Alexander the Great died, his empire was divided by his four generals into four quadrants, and they carried through that Greek Hellenization of the civilized world.

Aleksanda alipokufa akiwa na umri wa miaka thelathini na mitatu, alikuwa na umri ule ule wa Bwana wetu. Aleksanda Mkuu alipokufa, dola yake iligawanywa na majemadari wake wanne katika sehemu nne, nao waliendeleza ueneaji ule wa utamaduni wa Kigiriki (Uhelenisti) katika ulimwengu uliostaarabika.
In Egypt, in 280 BC, the Bible of the Hebrews was translated into Greek, into the Septuagint, and that was the same Bible that the first apostles and Christ used.
Huko Misri, mwaka 280 K.K., Biblia ya Waebrania ilitafsiriwa kwa Kigiriki, yaani Septuajinti, na hiyo ndiyo Biblia ile ile waliyoitumia mitume wa kwanza na Kristo.

When the Christian preachers and the evangelists went forth, declaring the wondrous works of God in Christ Jesus, they spoke in the universal language. From one side to the other they preached in Greek, and the whole world could understand. When Paul wrote his letter to the great capital city at Rome, called the Book of Romans, he wrote it in Greek. And when the apostle John wrote his letters to the seven churches of Asia, he wrote them in Greek. From one extremity of the empire to the other, it was Greek.

Wahubiri na wainjilisti Wakristo walipotoka kwenda kutangaza matendo makuu ya Mungu katika Kristo Yesu, walizungumza kwa lugha ya ulimwengu wote. Kutoka upande mmoja hadi mwingine walihubiri kwa Kigiriki, na ulimwengu wote uliweza kuelewa. Paulo alipoandika barua yake kwa mji mkuu mashuhuri wa Rumi, inayoitwa Kitabu cha Warumi, aliiandika kwa Kigiriki. Na mtume Yohana alipoandika barua zake kwa makanisa saba ya Asia, aliziandika kwa Kigiriki. Kutoka mwisho mmoja wa dola hadi mwisho mwingine, ilikuwa Kigiriki.

And those first Christian preachers, soulwinners, proclaimers of the wonderful grace of God, when they stood anywhere in the civilized world, they could be understood and they could hear Greek. Little did Alexander the Great or his successors dream that in building a Greek empire they were preparing the way, the plerōma, for the grace of God in the coming of Christ Jesus. "In the fullness of the time, God sent forth His Son, born of a woman"[Galatians 4:4].

Na wale wahubiri Wakristo wa kwanza, wavuvi wa roho, watangazaji wa neema ya ajabu ya Mungu, waliposimama mahali popote katika ulimwengu uliostaarabika, waliweza kueleweka na watu waliweza kusikia Kigiriki. Aleksanda Mkuu wala waliomfuata hawakuota hata kidogo kwamba kwa kujenga dola ya Kigiriki walikuwa wakiandaa njia, plerōma, kwa ajili ya neema ya Mungu katika kuja kwa Kristo Yesu. "Hata ulipowadia utimilifu wa wakati, Mungu alimtuma Mwanawe, amezaliwa na mwanamke"[Wagalatia 4:4].
D. Roman Peace.

Most people in the Mediterranean world were grateful to Rome. You could go from one side of the Empire to the other. The Romans rid the whole world of pirates on the sea and robbers on the land so that merchants and people could travel from one side to the other without fear of molestation. They did not need to fear robbers or invading armies. There was peace in the lands. The Romans also laced the entire civilized world with Roman roads. They are traveled on even today, those paved roads. And they inaugurated the finest postal service that the earth had ever known so that letters could be written and carried in dispatch all over the known world. And they brought to the world the Pax Romana, the universal peace.

Watu wengi katika ulimwengu wa Bahari ya Mediterania waliishukuru Rumi. Uliweza kusafiri kutoka upande mmoja wa Dola hadi mwingine. Warumi waliusafisha ulimwengu wote kutokana na maharamia baharini na wanyang'anyi nchi kavu, ili wafanyabiashara na watu wengine waweze kusafiri kutoka upande mmoja hadi mwingine bila hofu ya kushambuliwa. Hawakuhitaji kuogopa wanyang'anyi wala majeshi ya uvamizi. Kulikuwa na amani katika nchi. Warumi pia waliujaza ulimwengu wote uliostaarabika barabara za Kirumi. Bado zinatumiwa hata leo, barabara zile zilizojengwa kwa mawe. Nao walianzisha huduma bora kabisa ya posta ambayo dunia ilikuwa haijawahi kuijua, ili barua ziweze kuandikwa na kupelekwa haraka katika ulimwengu wote uliojulikana. Little did any Caesar ever realize, that what he was doing in building the Empire, he was making ready, and making way for the coming of the preaching of Jesus our Lord; a miracle of God’s grace.

8.1 Collecting Ideas and Materials
8.1 Kukusanya Mawazo na Vifaa

Specific preparation is the preparation that you do in your weekly routine. Many preachers find weekly sermon preparation exhausting. Reader's Digest once interviewed a preacher who quit because "the Sabbath came too often." Perhaps the Sabbath will not be such a dreaded day if you build sermon preparation into your routine. There are several steps:

Maandalizi mahususi ni maandalizi unayoyafanya katika utaratibu wako wa kila juma. Wahubiri wengi huona maandalizi ya mahubiri ya kila juma kuwa yanachosha sana. Gazeti la Reader's Digest liliwahi kumhoji mhubiri mmoja aliyeacha kazi kwa sababu "Sabato ilikuja mara nyingi mno." Huenda Sabato isiwe siku ya kuogopwa hivyo ikiwa utayaweka maandalizi ya mahubiri ndani ya utaratibu wako. Kuna hatua kadhaa:

1. Get the idea. Most pastors have difficulty here, and many seem to get the idea from the calendar and the clock. The idea may come from the text, a situation, a need, or a thought that pops into the mind. If you cannot find a text that has the idea you wish to use, it may not be Biblical and should not be preached. Some pastors plan their preaching for a year or so in advance by setting aside a few days for a retreat or study. Keep a sermon pad in your pocket — an idea may come while visiting or while attending a conference. Do not risk losing a good idea. 2. Study the text. Read it and reflect on it. Read the Bible both devotionally and exegetically. Some suggest reading a passage several times before starting to work with it. If you work through books of the Bible by systematic analysis, outlines will emerge naturally from your weekly study pattern. 3. Put down everything. Let your mind be creative. No matter how far-fetched an idea may seem, put it down. Sometimes a large drafting sheet helps for initial brainstorming. 4. Start collecting material. Have the idea at least one week in advance — preferably three months to a year. Some pastors keep 104 folders for upcoming sermon topics; as illustrations and information cross their desks, they drop them in the right folder. When the week arrives, the folder already contains much of the work. 5. Gather other materials. Several Bible translations and paraphrases, linguistic tools (Vine's, Wuest, Barclay for word studies), concordances (Strong's, Young's), commentaries (one or two critical sets such as Word and Interpreter's; devotional authors such as Barclay, McGee, Gutzke, Wiersbe — buy by author, not by set), Bible dictionaries (Interpreter's, Zondervan's Pictorial Encyclopedia), and a thematic index for topical references.

1. Pata wazo. Wachungaji wengi hupata shida hapa, na wengi huonekana kupata wazo kutoka kwenye kalenda na saa. Wazo linaweza kutoka kwenye kifungu cha Maandiko, hali fulani, hitaji, au fikra inayokujia akilini ghafla. Ikiwa huwezi kupata kifungu chenye wazo unalotaka kulitumia, huenda wazo hilo si la Kibiblia na halipaswi kuhubiriwa. Wachungaji wengine hupanga mahubiri yao kwa mwaka mmoja hivi kabla, kwa kutenga siku chache za mapumziko ya kiroho au za kujifunza. Weka kijitabu cha kuandikia mahubiri mfukoni mwako — wazo linaweza kukujia ukiwa unatembelea watu au ukihudhuria mkutano. Usihatarishe kupoteza wazo zuri.
2. Jifunze kifungu. Kisome na ukitafakari. Soma Biblia kwa njia ya ibada binafsi na pia kwa njia ya ufafanuzi wa kina (eksejesia). Wengine hushauri kusoma kifungu mara kadhaa kabla ya kuanza kukifanyia kazi. Ukipitia vitabu vya Biblia kwa uchambuzi wa utaratibu, mihtasari itajitokeza yenyewe kutokana na mpangilio wako wa kujifunza kila juma.
3. Andika kila kitu. Iache akili yako iwe bunifu. Hata kama wazo linaonekana kuwa la mbali kiasi gani, liandike. Wakati mwingine karatasi kubwa ya kuchorea husaidia katika hatua ya kwanza ya kubungua bongo (kutoa mawazo kwa uhuru).
4. Anza kukusanya vifaa. Uwe na wazo angalau juma moja kabla — ikiwezekana miezi mitatu hadi mwaka mmoja. Wachungaji wengine huweka mafaili 104 kwa ajili ya mada za mahubiri yanayokuja; kadiri vielelezo na habari vinavyopita mezani pao, huviweka katika faili linalofaa. Juma linapofika, faili tayari lina sehemu kubwa ya kazi.
5. Kusanya vifaa vingine. Tafsiri kadhaa za Biblia na tafsiri za maneno huru (paraphrase), vitendea kazi vya lugha (Vine's, Wuest, Barclay kwa ajili ya kujifunza maneno), konkodansi (Strong's, Young's), vitabu vya maelezo/fafanuzi (seti moja au mbili za kitaaluma kama Word na Interpreter's; waandishi wa kiibada kama Barclay, McGee, Gutzke, Wiersbe — nunua kwa kufuata mwandishi, si kwa seti), kamusi za Biblia (Interpreter's, Zondervan's Pictorial Encyclopedia), na faharasa ya mada kwa ajili ya marejeo ya kimada.
