6. Arrange the material. Put down a tentative outline. Note references and page numbers for ideas and illustrations you may use within the outline. Later you can type or write the other material into the sermon. 7. Brood over the message. Write down the important ideas. Make any changes in the outline or plan that you need to make. This is a place for imagination and style. 8. Write out the sermon with an oral style. Think of the words as they will sound. Write the body first, then the invitation, and only last the introduction — because the sermon often develops in a different direction than originally anticipated. 9. Prepare to preach. Most immediate preparation can be done on Sunday morning. Read through the sermon slowly; preach it through in your mind before breakfast. (a) Prayer. Spirit-filled sermons are not effortless to produce — they are bathed in fervent prayer. Preaching drives the preacher to his knees with inadequacy more than anything else. (b) Studying and restudying. A sermon is always fresher if it has been working in your soul all week. (c) Go over the sermon on your feet at least twice. Once before the mirror; once in the pastor's study during the first part of Sunday School.

6. Panga vifaa. Andika muhtasari wa awali. Andika marejeo na namba za kurasa za mawazo na vielelezo unavyoweza kutumia ndani ya muhtasari. Baadaye unaweza kuchapa au kuandika vifaa vingine ndani ya mahubiri.
7. Tafakari ujumbe kwa kina. Andika mawazo muhimu. Fanya mabadiliko yoyote unayohitaji katika muhtasari au mpango. Hapa ndipo mahali pa ubunifu wa fikra na mtindo.
8. Andika mahubiri kwa mtindo wa kuzungumza. Yafikirie maneno jinsi yatakavyosikika. Andika kiini (mwili) kwanza, kisha mwaliko, na mwisho kabisa utangulizi — kwa sababu mara nyingi mahubiri hukua kuelekea upande tofauti na ule uliotarajiwa mwanzoni.
9. Jiandae kuhubiri. Maandalizi mengi ya karibu yanaweza kufanyika Jumapili asubuhi. Soma mahubiri polepole; yahubiri akilini mwako kabla ya kifungua kinywa. (a) Maombi. Mahubiri yaliyojaa Roho Mtakatifu hayatengenezwi bila juhudi — yamelowekwa katika maombi ya bidii. Kuhubiri humpeleka mhubiri magotini kwa hisia ya kutotosha kuliko jambo lingine lolote. (b) Kujifunza na kujifunza tena. Mahubiri huwa mapya zaidi kila mara ikiwa yamekuwa yakifanya kazi nafsini mwako juma zima. (c) Yapitie mahubiri ukiwa umesimama angalau mara mbili. Mara moja mbele ya kioo; mara moja katika ofisi ya mchungaji wakati wa sehemu ya kwanza ya Shule ya Jumapili.
8.3 Methods of Delivery
8.3 Njia za Uwasilishaji

John Basigno says that two things are important in preaching: delivery and content. He gives the example of the big league baseball player who earns a huge salary by pitching an inexpensive baseball — the minor leaguer pitches the same ball for a fraction of the salary. The difference is not the baseball but the delivery. A sermon is not a sermon until it has been heard. There are five methods of delivery, and no one method fits everyone — each preacher should discover the way that is most effective for his own gifts.

John Basigno anasema mambo mawili ni muhimu katika kuhubiri: uwasilishaji na maudhui. Anatoa mfano wa mchezaji wa ligi kuu ya besiboli anayelipwa mshahara mkubwa sana kwa kurusha mpira wa besiboli wa bei nafuu — mchezaji wa ligi ndogo hurusha mpira uleule kwa sehemu ndogo tu ya mshahara huo. Tofauti si mpira bali ni urushaji (uwasilishaji). Mahubiri si mahubiri mpaka yamesikika. Kuna njia tano za uwasilishaji, na hakuna njia moja inayomfaa kila mtu — kila mhubiri anapaswa kugundua njia iliyo na matokeo bora zaidi kwa karama zake mwenyewe.

1. Memorizing. The sermon is written in full and then committed to memory. Very stressful — if one word is forgotten, the preacher may get lost. 2. Reading. The sermon is written beforehand, the notes are carried to the pulpit, and the sermon is read. Jonathan Edwards, Thomas Chalmers, and Peter Marshall all used this method. Not the most popular method, especially in a free-church tradition — many laymen say, "If he is going to read it, he might as well give me the copy and let me read it." 3. Extemporaneous. Preaching without notes or with very limited notes. John Basigno, Norman Vincent Peale, Clarence McCartney, Charles Koller, and V. L. Stanfield all advocate this method. Stanfield calls it "free delivery" — careful preparation, but no notes. Many preachers find it liberating after years of being tied to a manuscript. 4. Limited Notes. Either a brief outline or a highlighted manuscript is carried to the pulpit. Best only for those who can use notes without being tied to them. 5. Impromptu. Speaking at the spur of the moment with limited preparation. Spurgeon sometimes employed something akin to this and succeeded admirably, but it can lead to blunders. Some independent-fundamentalist Baptist preachers once believed it unspiritual to prepare a sermon at all; they tended to be long-winded and repetitious. Do not try to speak impromptu unless you have developed a pronounced talent for this method.

1. Kukariri. Mahubiri huandikwa kikamilifu kisha hukaririwa. Ni njia yenye msongo mkubwa — ikiwa neno moja litasahaulika, mhubiri anaweza kupotea.
2. Kusoma. Mahubiri huandikwa mapema, maandishi hupelekwa mimbarini, na mahubiri husomwa. Jonathan Edwards, Thomas Chalmers, na Peter Marshall wote walitumia njia hii. Si njia inayopendwa zaidi, hasa katika mapokeo ya makanisa huru — waumini wengi wa kawaida husema, "Kama atayasoma, afadhali anipe nakala nami niisome mwenyewe."
3. Bila mswada (extemporaneous). Kuhubiri bila maandishi au kwa maandishi machache sana. John Basigno, Norman Vincent Peale, Clarence McCartney, Charles Koller, na V. L. Stanfield wote wanaitetea njia hii. Stanfield anaiita "uwasilishaji huru" — maandalizi makini, lakini bila maandishi. Wahubiri wengi huiona kuwa yenye kuwaweka huru baada ya miaka mingi ya kufungwa kwenye mswada.
4. Maandishi Machache. Muhtasari mfupi au mswada uliowekewa alama hupelekwa mimbarini. Inafaa zaidi kwa wale tu wanaoweza kutumia maandishi bila kufungwa nayo.
5. Papo kwa papo (bila maandalizi). Kuzungumza kwa ghafla na kwa maandalizi kidogo. Spurgeon wakati mwingine alitumia kitu kinachofanana na hiki na akafanikiwa sana, lakini kinaweza kuleta makosa makubwa. Baadhi ya wahubiri wa Kibaptisti wa kujitegemea wenye msimamo mkali wa kimsingi (fundamentalist) waliwahi kuamini kuwa si jambo la kiroho kuandaa mahubiri hata kidogo; walielekea kuwa wa maneno marefu na wa kurudiarudia. Usijaribu kuzungumza papo kwa papo isipokuwa umekuza kipaji cha wazi cha njia hii.
8.4 Five Half-Truths About Delivery
8.4 Nusu-Kweli Tano Kuhusu Uwasilishaji
Robert Kirkpatrick warned of five common but incomplete pieces of advice:
Robert Kirkpatrick alionya kuhusu mashauri matano yaliyozoeleka lakini yasiyo kamili:

1. "Be natural." The call for naturalness is a reaction against the old preacher's horn — a monotone yelling. The problem is that some people are naturally dull. Preaching is an art and naturally bad habits need correcting. Preaching is to be conversational in manner, but not in emphasis or volume. 2. "Learn to use your body and voice correctly." Too much emphasis on technique can be stifling. The time to focus on techniques is before delivery — during the sermon, allow it to flow unhindered. 3. "Be filled with your subject." You may be so filled with the subject that you forget the object — the audience. Watch for cues: coughing, fidgeting, upright heads, and yawning signal inattention; enthusiastic singing, slightly tilted heads, frequent blinking, smiling and nodding signal engagement. 4. "Desire to help others." The desire to help is no guarantee of effectiveness. Earnest desire cannot overcome defects of style and delivery. Some very sincere preachers are incompetent communicators. 5. "God will provide." God does provide, but rarely when the preacher has not made effort beforehand. As Kirkpatrick said: "It is no more sensible for a preacher to expect a miraculous gift of speech than for a missionary to go to the heathen expecting to receive the gift of tongues."

1. "Kuwa wa kawaida (wa asili)." Wito wa kuwa wa asili ni mwitikio dhidi ya "tarumbeta ya mhubiri" wa zamani — kupiga kelele kwa sauti moja isiyobadilika. Tatizo ni kwamba baadhi ya watu kwa asili ni wachoshi. Kuhubiri ni sanaa, na tabia mbaya za asili zinahitaji kurekebishwa. Kuhubiri kunapaswa kuwa na namna ya mazungumzo, lakini si katika msisitizo wala ukubwa wa sauti.
2. "Jifunze kutumia mwili na sauti yako kwa usahihi." Kusisitiza mbinu kupita kiasi kunaweza kukandamiza. Wakati wa kuzingatia mbinu ni kabla ya uwasilishaji — wakati wa mahubiri, yaache yatiririke bila kizuizi.
3. "Jaa somo lako." Unaweza kujawa na somo kiasi kwamba unalisahau lengo — yaani wasikilizaji. Angalia ishara: kukohoa, kuhangaika, vichwa vilivyosimama wima, na kupiga miayo huonyesha kutokuwa makini; kuimba kwa shauku, vichwa vilivyoinama kidogo, kupepesa macho mara kwa mara, kutabasamu na kutikisa vichwa kukubali huonyesha usikivu.
4. "Tamani kuwasaidia wengine." Tamaa ya kusaidia si hakikisho la kuwa na matokeo. Tamaa ya dhati haiwezi kushinda kasoro za mtindo na uwasilishaji. Baadhi ya wahubiri wenye moyo mnyoofu sana ni wawasilishaji wasio na uwezo.
5. "Mungu atatoa." Mungu hutoa kweli, lakini mara chache sana ikiwa mhubiri hajafanya juhudi kabla. Kama Kirkpatrick alivyosema: "Si busara zaidi kwa mhubiri kutarajia karama ya miujiza ya kuzungumza kuliko kwa mmisionari kwenda kwa wapagani akitarajia kupokea karama ya lugha."
8.5 Verbal Aspects of Delivery
8.5 Vipengele vya Sauti katika Uwasilishaji

Voice projection and volume. Aim the voice slightly upward about ten feet above the congregation. One preacher spoke to a nail on the back wall. Volume should usually begin low — the introduction does not call for a lot of volume. The old black preachers' advice: "Start slow. Stay low. Get higher. Catch fire." At times be loud; at other times speak softly and use a pause of four to five seconds after a profound statement.

Kutoa sauti na ukubwa wa sauti. Ielekeze sauti juu kidogo, karibu futi kumi (takriban mita tatu) juu ya kusanyiko. Mhubiri mmoja alizungumza akilenga msumari kwenye ukuta wa nyuma. Kwa kawaida ukubwa wa sauti unapaswa kuanza chini — utangulizi hauhitaji sauti kubwa sana. Ushauri wa wahubiri weusi wa zamani: "Anza polepole. Kaa chini. Panda juu. Waka moto." Wakati mwingine piga sauti kubwa; wakati mwingine zungumza kwa upole na utumie kituo cha sekunde nne hadi tano baada ya kauli nzito.

Pitch, tone, and inflection. Find your optimum pitch level (about three to five notes above the lowest note you can hit). Three kinds of inflection: downward for a completed thought, upward for question or excitement, circumflex (up and down) for strong doubt or emphasis. Reading fairy tales to children improves inflection — we are naturally expressive with children but inhibited with adults. Beware of raising pitch as volume increases; consciously reach down for a lower note when getting louder.

Kiwango cha sauti, toni, na kiimbo. Tafuta kiwango chako bora cha sauti (karibu noti tatu hadi tano juu ya noti ya chini kabisa unayoweza kuifikia). Aina tatu za kiimbo: kushuka kwa wazo lililokamilika, kupanda kwa swali au msisimko, kupanda-na-kushuka (circumflex) kwa shaka kubwa au msisitizo. Kuwasomea watoto hadithi za ngano huboresha kiimbo — kwa asili sisi huonyesha hisia kwa urahisi tukiwa na watoto lakini tunajizuia tukiwa na watu wazima. Jihadhari na kupandisha kiwango cha sauti kadiri ukubwa wa sauti unavyoongezeka; kwa makusudi shuka kwenye noti ya chini zaidi unapoongeza sauti.

Rate. Two dangers — speaking too rapidly (nervousness) and speaking too slowly (a greater danger). Faster talkers (around 180 words per minute) are more persuasive than slow or average ones (120-150). A rate twenty to twenty-five percent above average is ideal. The pause can be very effective — Jack Benny would pause before his punch line much longer than other comedians. Use pauses for punctuation, effect, and emphasis. Pause for a moment before beginning to speak; this focuses the audience's attention on you.

Kasi. Hatari mbili — kuzungumza haraka mno (wasiwasi) na kuzungumza polepole mno (hatari kubwa zaidi). Wanaozungumza kwa kasi zaidi (karibu maneno 180 kwa dakika) huwashawishi watu zaidi kuliko wale wa polepole au wa wastani (120-150). Kasi ya asilimia ishirini hadi ishirini na tano juu ya wastani ndiyo bora. Kituo (kunyamaza kidogo) kinaweza kuwa na nguvu sana — Jack Benny alinyamaza kabla ya kusema kichekesho chake cha mwisho kwa muda mrefu zaidi kuliko wachekeshaji wengine. Tumia vituo kama alama za uakifishaji, kwa ajili ya athari, na kwa msisitizo. Nyamaza kwa muda mfupi kabla ya kuanza kuzungumza; jambo hili huelekeza usikivu wa wasikilizaji kwako.

Conversational voice and enthusiasm. A good speech is the projection of a good conversation. The monotone yell is the greatest danger to conversational speech. The one characteristic all the great preachers share is enthusiasm — sometimes called zeal, unction, fire, energy. It is not the same as volume, nor as oratory. Most students rate their energy too high; on videotape what felt like a six or seven shows as a two or three. "Preaching from the soul" and "dominating the space" both describe enthusiasm — the preacher's presence occupies all the space he and the audience share.

Sauti ya mazungumzo na shauku. Hotuba nzuri ni upanuzi wa mazungumzo mazuri. Kupiga kelele kwa sauti moja isiyobadilika ndiyo hatari kubwa zaidi kwa usemi wa mazungumzo. Sifa moja ambayo wahubiri wote wakuu wanashiriki ni shauku — wakati mwingine huitwa bidii, upako, moto, nguvu. Si sawa na ukubwa wa sauti, wala si sawa na ufasaha wa hotuba. Wanafunzi wengi hukadiria nguvu zao kuwa juu mno; kwenye video, kile kilichoonekana kama sita au saba huonekana kama mbili au tatu. "Kuhubiri kutoka nafsini" na "kutawala nafasi" vyote vinaeleza shauku — uwepo wa mhubiri hujaza nafasi yote ambayo yeye na wasikilizaji wanashiriki.
8.6 The Body in Delivery
8.6 Mwili katika Uwasilishaji

Albert Mehrabian's research suggests communication is seven percent verbal, thirty-eight percent vocal, and fifty-five percent facial. If words and actions disagree, we tend to believe the actions. Six elements:

Utafiti wa Albert Mehrabian unaonyesha kwamba mawasiliano ni asilimia saba maneno, asilimia thelathini na nane sauti, na asilimia hamsini na tano uso. Maneno na matendo yasipokubaliana, huelekea kuamini matendo. Vipengele sita:

1. Authority and confidence. People look for a father figure in a leader. Fear is the great enemy of confidence — fidgeting, rattling change in your pocket, clearing the throat, foot shuffling, stammering, "ah" and "you know" all display lack of poise. Control nervous habits with deep breaths and finger-shaking before the service. Speak with the authority of Scripture — avoid "to my limited knowledge…" or "I don't have all the facts, but…" Billy Graham's "the Bible says…" is very effective. 2. General appearance. The minister's appearance should not call attention to itself. A business suit usually fits, though some preachers targeting younger audiences dress casually. Enter the pulpit with dignity and poise. Take a firm stand a short distance from the pulpit. Do not lean on it or grip its edges — the pulpit is for the Bible and your notes, not to hold you up. 3. Movement. A small pulpit and a lapel mike free movement. Slightly forward is psychologically preferred to a backward defensive hesitation. Some pastors preach the entire sermon in front of the pulpit. Avoid quick jerky movements from nervousness. 4. The face. Smile while preaching; the face needs to appear as though we are delivering the most important message of the hour. Eyebrows raised and lowered; eyes twinkling. Avoid a dead-pan poker face unless delivering a funeral eulogy. 5. Eye contact. Look at the audience constantly. Look at individuals, not at a mass. Maintain contact with some person all the time. Audiences strongly prefer good eye contact. 6. The hands. The hands enhance or detract. Pulling at the ear, twiddling thumbs, stroking a tie or playing with keys disconcerts the audience. When not in use let the hands drop by the side — they will be there when needed. Cultivate gestures: hands, face, and eyes should work together. Above all — sincerity — delivery begins with the personality. Genuine sincerity comes across.

1. Mamlaka na kujiamini. Watu hutafuta sura ya baba katika kiongozi. Hofu ni adui mkubwa wa kujiamini — kuhangaika, kuchezesha sarafu mfukoni, kukohoa ili kusafisha koo, kuburuta miguu, kugugumiza, "aa" na "unajua" vyote huonyesha ukosefu wa utulivu. Dhibiti tabia za wasiwasi kwa kuvuta pumzi ndefu na kutikisa vidole kabla ya ibada. Zungumza kwa mamlaka ya Maandiko — epuka "kwa ufahamu wangu mdogo…" au "sina habari zote, lakini…" Usemi wa Billy Graham "Biblia inasema…" una matokeo makubwa sana.
2. Mwonekano wa jumla. Mwonekano wa mhudumu haupaswi kujivutia wenyewe. Kwa kawaida suti ya kikazi inafaa, ingawa baadhi ya wahubiri wanaolenga wasikilizaji vijana huvaa nguo za kawaida. Ingia mimbarini kwa heshima na utulivu. Simama imara umbali mfupi kutoka kwenye mimbari. Usiiegemee wala usiishike kingo zake — mimbari ni kwa ajili ya Biblia na maandishi yako, si kwa ajili ya kukushikilia usimame.
3. Mwendo. Mimbari ndogo na kipaza sauti cha kubana kwenye nguo huruhusu kutembea kwa uhuru. Kusogea mbele kidogo hupendelewa kisaikolojia kuliko kusita kwa kurudi nyuma kwa kujihami. Wachungaji wengine huhubiri mahubiri yote wakiwa mbele ya mimbari. Epuka miondoko ya haraka ya kushtuka inayotokana na wasiwasi.
4. Uso. Tabasamu unapohubiri; uso unahitaji kuonekana kana kwamba tunawasilisha ujumbe muhimu kuliko yote wa saa hiyo. Nyusi zipande na kushuka; macho yang'ae. Epuka uso mkavu usioonyesha hisia yoyote isipokuwa unapotoa hotuba ya kumsifu marehemu katika mazishi.
5. Kuwatazama machoni. Watazame wasikilizaji muda wote. Watazame watu mmoja mmoja, si umati. Dumisha kumtazama mtu fulani wakati wote. Wasikilizaji hupendelea sana kutazamwa machoni vizuri.
6. Mikono. Mikono huongeza au hupunguza. Kuvuta sikio, kuzungusha vidole gumba, kupapasa tai au kuchezea funguo huwavuruga wasikilizaji. Usipoitumia, iache mikono ining'inie pembeni mwako — itakuwepo utakapoihitaji. Kuza ishara za mwili: mikono, uso, na macho vinapaswa kufanya kazi pamoja. Zaidi ya yote — unyoofu wa moyo — uwasilishaji huanza na utu wa mtu. Unyoofu wa kweli huonekana wazi.
Unit Nine · Stage 3: Learn from the Masters
Sehemu ya Tisa · Hatua ya 3: Jifunze kutoka kwa Mabingwa
Four Great Centuries of Preaching
Karne Nne Kuu za Kuhubiri

Some students of church history have observed that there are four great centuries of preaching — the first, the fourth, the sixteenth, and the nineteenth. Each century answered a different crisis; each gave us preachers whose voices still teach us how to preach.

Baadhi ya wanafunzi wa historia ya kanisa wameona kwamba kuna karne nne kuu za kuhubiri — ya kwanza, ya nne, ya kumi na sita, na ya kumi na tisa. Kila karne ilijibu mgogoro tofauti; kila moja ilitupa wahubiri ambao sauti zao bado zinatufundisha jinsi ya kuhubiri.
9.1 Why Study the Preachers
9.1 Kwa Nini Tujifunze Habari za Wahubiri

Studying great preachers is studying great preaching in action. A textbook gives you the parts of a sermon; a great preacher shows you how the parts move when a soul is in the balance. You have learned, in the first seven units of this course, every skill the discipline of homiletics has to offer: text selection, the probing question, divisions and movement, induction, application and illustration, beauty and simplicity, delivery. Now we put those tools down for a unit and watch the masters work.

Kujifunza habari za wahubiri wakuu ni kujifunza mahubiri makuu yakiwa kazini. Kitabu cha kiada kinakupa sehemu za hotuba ya mahubiri; mhubiri mkuu anakuonyesha jinsi sehemu hizo zinavyosonga wakati nafsi ya mtu iko hatarini. Katika sehemu saba za kwanza za kozi hii, umejifunza kila ujuzi ambao taaluma ya elimu ya kuhubiri (homiletiki) inaweza kutoa: kuchagua kifungu, swali la kuchunguza, migawanyo na mwendo, njia ya kujenga hoja kuanzia mifano (induction), matumizi na kielelezo, uzuri na urahisi, na uwasilishaji. Sasa tunaweka zana hizo chini kwa muda wa sehemu moja na kuwatazama mabingwa wakifanya kazi.

There is an old observation among church historians that, while preaching has continued without break for two thousand years, four centuries stand out as great pulpit eras. The first century gave us the apostolic preaching of Jesus and the apostles. The fourth century gave us the Christian rhetoric of Chrysostom and Augustine. The sixteenth century gave us the Reformers. The nineteenth century gave us a flowering of evangelistic and pastoral pulpits that still shapes us. Other centuries had great preachers too — Savonarola in the fifteenth, Wesley and Whitefield in the eighteenth, Graham in the twentieth — but these four are the high water marks. We will visit each in turn.

Kuna maoni ya zamani miongoni mwa wanahistoria wa kanisa kwamba, ingawa kuhubiri kumeendelea bila kukatika kwa miaka elfu mbili, karne nne zinajitokeza kama nyakati kuu za mimbari. Karne ya kwanza ilitupa mahubiri ya kitume ya Yesu na mitume. Karne ya nne ilitupa balagha ya Kikristo ya Krisostomo na Augustino. Karne ya kumi na sita ilitupa Wanamatengenezo. Karne ya kumi na tisa ilitupa kuchanua kwa mimbari za kiinjilisti na za kichungaji ambazo bado zinatuunda. Karne nyingine pia zilikuwa na wahubiri wakuu — Savonarola katika karne ya kumi na tano, Wesley na Whitefield katika karne ya kumi na nane, Graham katika karne ya ishirini — lakini hizi nne ndizo vilele vya juu kabisa. Tutazitembelea moja baada ya nyingine.
9.2 The First Century: Turning the World Upside Down
9.2 Karne ya Kwanza: Kuipindua Dunia

When the believers reached Thessalonica, their enemies complained to the city officials with a phrase that has rung through every great revival since: "These who have turned the world upside down have come here too" (Acts 17:6). It was meant as an accusation; the church has worn it as a badge. How did a handful of Galilean fishermen and one converted Pharisee turn over the Roman world in a single generation? They preached.

Waamini walipofika Thesalonike, adui zao walilalamika kwa wakuu wa mji kwa maneno ambayo yamevuma katika kila uamsho mkuu tangu wakati huo: "Watu hawa waliopindua dunia wamefika huku nao" (Matendo 17:6). Yalikusudiwa kuwa shtaka; kanisa limeyavaa kama nishani ya heshima. Ni jinsi gani kikundi kidogo cha wavuvi wa Galilaya na Farisayo mmoja aliyeongoka walivyoupindua ulimwengu wa Kirumi katika kizazi kimoja tu? Walihubiri.

Jesus is the Master Preacher and the model by which all others are measured. He preached with an authority the crowds had never heard. The Sermon on the Mount opens with the Beatitudes and proceeds through six "you have heard it said... but I say to you" antitheses (Matthew 5–7) — He claims the right to interpret Moses with His own voice. His parables turn the sermon into story; the Prodigal Son, the Good Samaritan, the Sower, and the Pearl of Great Price are still the most quoted illustrations in the world. And He balanced the public crowd with the private disciple — the same lips that fed five thousand on a Galilean hillside took thirteen men aside in an upper room and washed their feet.

Yesu ndiye Mhubiri Mkuu na kipimo ambacho wengine wote hupimwa nacho. Alihubiri kwa mamlaka ambayo makutano hawakuwahi kuyasikia. Mahubiri ya Mlimani yanaanza na Heri, kisha yanaendelea kupitia tofauti sita za "Mmesikia kwamba imenenwa... lakini mimi nawaambia" (Mathayo 5–7) — Yeye anadai haki ya kumfasiri Musa kwa sauti yake mwenyewe. Mifano yake hugeuza mahubiri kuwa hadithi; Mwana Mpotevu, Msamaria Mwema, Mpanzi, na Lulu ya Thamani Kubwa bado ndivyo vielelezo vinavyonukuliwa zaidi duniani. Tena alisawazisha makutano ya hadharani na mwanafunzi wa faragha — midomo ile ile iliyowalisha watu elfu tano kwenye kilima cha Galilaya iliwachukua wanaume kumi na watatu kando katika chumba cha juu na kuwaosha miguu.

Peter is the apostolic example of preaching under the Spirit's anointing. On the day of Pentecost, having denied his Lord less than two months before, he stood up with the eleven and preached one sermon — and three thousand were saved (Acts 2). It was not eloquence; it was Scripture. He quoted Joel, he quoted David's Psalms, and he proclaimed Jesus crucified and risen. A few weeks later at Solomon's Portico, with a lame man healed at his side, he preached again and another five thousand believed (Acts 3–4). Peter's preaching is what Spirit-filled, Scripture-saturated proclamation looks like when no skill on earth can explain the result.

Petro ni kielelezo cha kitume cha kuhubiri chini ya upako wa Roho. Siku ya Pentekoste, akiwa amemkana Bwana wake chini ya miezi miwili kabla, alisimama pamoja na wale kumi na mmoja akahubiri hotuba moja ya mahubiri — na watu elfu tatu wakaokoka (Matendo 2). Haikuwa ufasaha wa maneno; yalikuwa Maandiko. Alimnukuu Yoeli, alinukuu Zaburi za Daudi, na akamtangaza Yesu aliyesulibiwa na kufufuka. Majuma machache baadaye katika ukumbi wa Sulemani, akiwa na kiwete aliyeponywa kando yake, alihubiri tena na wengine elfu tano wakaamini (Matendo 3–4). Mahubiri ya Petro ndiyo jinsi utangazaji uliojaa Roho na kujaa Maandiko unavyoonekana pale ambapo hakuna ujuzi wowote wa duniani unaoweza kueleza matokeo yake.

Paul is the missionary preacher, the apologist, and the church's foremost writer of preached theology. On Mars Hill in Athens he stood among the philosophers and built a bridge from their "altar to the Unknown God" straight to the resurrection of Christ (Acts 17). His thirteen epistles are sermons in letter form — they were read aloud to the gathered churches and still preach with the freshness of the day they were written. Paul shows us that the preacher must engage the culture without surrendering the gospel, and that written preaching is preaching too: the page is a pulpit when the words have been forged in love and fire.

Paulo ni mhubiri wa kimisionari, mtetezi wa imani, na mwandishi mkuu wa kanisa wa theolojia iliyohubiriwa. Juu ya kilima cha Areopago (Mars Hill) huko Athene alisimama miongoni mwa wanafalsafa na akajenga daraja kutoka "madhabahu yao kwa Mungu Asiyejulikana" moja kwa moja hadi ufufuo wa Kristo (Matendo 17). Nyaraka zake kumi na tatu ni mahubiri katika umbo la barua — zilisomwa kwa sauti kwa makanisa yaliyokusanyika na bado zinahubiri kwa upya ule ule wa siku zilipoandikwa. Paulo anatuonyesha kwamba mhubiri lazima ajihusishe na utamaduni bila kuisalimisha injili, na kwamba kuhubiri kwa maandishi nako ni kuhubiri: ukurasa ni mimbari pale maneno yamefuliwa katika upendo na moto.

And then there is Stephen, the deacon, who preached the sermon that cost him his life (Acts 7). Charged before the Sanhedrin, he answered with a sweeping survey of redemptive history — Abraham, Joseph, Moses, David, Solomon — and closed by pointing to Jesus as the Righteous One they had murdered. The stones started flying before the closing prayer. Stephen reminds us that not every faithful sermon ends in revival. Some end in stones. And in the front row of those who heard him died was a young Pharisee named Saul of Tarsus, who would one day stand on Mars Hill himself.

Kisha yupo Stefano, shemasi, aliyehubiri mahubiri yaliyomgharimu uhai wake (Matendo 7). Alipohukumiwa mbele ya Baraza (Sanhedrini), alijibu kwa mapitio mapana ya historia ya ukombozi — Ibrahimu, Yusufu, Musa, Daudi, Sulemani — na akamalizia kwa kumwelekeza Yesu kama yule Mwenye Haki waliyemwua. Mawe yalianza kurushwa kabla ya sala ya kufunga. Stefano anatukumbusha kwamba si kila mahubiri ya uaminifu huishia katika uamsho. Mengine huishia katika mawe. Na katika safu ya mbele ya wale waliomsikia akifa alikuwepo Farisayo kijana aitwaye Sauli wa Tarso, ambaye siku moja angesimama yeye mwenyewe juu ya Areopago.
9.3 The Fourth Century: The Patristic Pulpit
9.3 Karne ya Nne: Mimbari ya Mababa wa Kanisa

After Constantine's edict in A.D. 313, the church stepped out of the catacombs and into the basilicas. For the first time in two and a half centuries, preachers preached in daylight and lived to preach again next week. Three centuries of underground catechesis had produced a generation of theologically prepared believers; now they needed pulpits worthy of them. The fourth century delivered.

Baada ya amri ya Konstantino mwaka 313 B.K., kanisa lilitoka katika makaburi ya chini ya ardhi (katakombu) na kuingia katika makanisa makubwa (basilika). Kwa mara ya kwanza katika karne mbili na nusu, wahubiri walihubiri mchana kweupe na wakaishi ili kuhubiri tena juma lililofuata. Karne tatu za mafundisho ya imani ya chinichini (katekesi) zilikuwa zimezalisha kizazi cha waamini waliotayarishwa kitheolojia; sasa walihitaji mimbari zinazowastahili. Karne ya nne ilizitoa.

John Chrysostom (c. 347–407) is the patron saint of expositors. Born in Antioch, trained as an orator under the pagan rhetorician Libanius, he was converted in his early twenties and gave away his fortune to live as a monk. When the church called him back to the city, he became a presbyter at Antioch and preached so powerfully that the city named him Chrysostomos — "Golden Mouth." He preached straight through whole books of Scripture in series after series, verse by verse, with a clarity that congregations could follow and a courage that emperors could not bear. In 397 he was made bishop of Constantinople, the capital itself, and immediately turned the pulpit against the worldliness of the imperial court. The Empress Eudoxia banished him for it. He died in exile in 407, still walking to the next assigned village. Hundreds of his sermons survive — they remain among the most exegetically careful and pastorally tender preaching ever written down.

Yohana Krisostomo (takriban 347–407) ni msimamizi mtakatifu wa wafafanuzi wa Maandiko. Alizaliwa Antiokia, akafundishwa kuwa msemaji hodari chini ya mtaalamu wa balagha mpagani Libanius; aliongoka akiwa na umri wa miaka ishirini na kitu, akatoa mali yake yote ili kuishi kama mtawa. Kanisa lilipomwita arudi mjini, alikuwa presbiteri (mzee wa kanisa) huko Antiokia na alihubiri kwa nguvu kiasi kwamba mji ulimpa jina Chrysostomos — "Kinywa cha Dhahabu." Alihubiri moja kwa moja kupitia vitabu vizima vya Maandiko, mfululizo baada ya mfululizo, mstari kwa mstari, kwa uwazi ambao makusanyiko yangeweza kuufuata na kwa ujasiri ambao wafalme hawakuweza kuuvumilia. Mwaka 397 alifanywa askofu wa Konstantinopo, mji mkuu wenyewe, na mara moja akaigeuza mimbari dhidi ya hali ya kidunia ya baraza la kifalme. Malkia Eudoxia alimfukuza uhamishoni kwa sababu hiyo. Alifia uhamishoni mwaka 407, akiwa bado anatembea kuelekea kijiji kingine alichopangiwa. Mamia ya mahubiri yake yamehifadhiwa — bado ni miongoni mwa mahubiri yaliyowahi kuandikwa yaliyo makini zaidi katika ufafanuzi wa kifungu na yenye upole zaidi wa kichungaji.

Augustine of Hippo (354–430) is the patron of theological preaching. A North African rhetorician who had pursued every passion of his age and found each one empty, he was converted in a garden in Milan in 386 reading Romans 13. He became bishop of the small port city of Hippo and stayed there forty years, preaching, writing, and shaping the theology of the Western church. His Confessions is the first spiritual autobiography in literature; his City of God is a theology of history written while Rome was sacked outside his city walls. He is believed to have preached around eight thousand sermons in his lifetime; some five hundred survive. And in Book IV of his On Christian Doctrine he gave the church its first preaching manual — a brilliant fusion of classical rhetoric and Christian content that argues the preacher must aim to teach, to delight, and to move, in that order. Every later preaching textbook, including this one, descends from that book.

Augustino wa Hippo (354–430) ni msimamizi wa kuhubiri kwa kitheolojia. Akiwa mtaalamu wa balagha kutoka Afrika Kaskazini aliyefuatilia kila tamaa ya zama zake na kuona kila moja ni tupu, aliongoka katika bustani huko Milano mwaka 386 alipokuwa akisoma Warumi 13. Akawa askofu wa mji mdogo wa bandari wa Hippo na akakaa huko miaka arobaini, akihubiri, akiandika, na kuunda theolojia ya kanisa la Magharibi. Kitabu chake Maungamo (Confessions) ni wasifu wa kwanza wa kiroho katika fasihi; kitabu chake Mji wa Mungu (City of God) ni theolojia ya historia iliyoandikwa wakati Roma ilipokuwa ikiporwa nje ya kuta za mji wake. Inaaminika kwamba alihubiri takriban mahubiri elfu nane katika maisha yake; karibu mia tano yamehifadhiwa. Na katika Kitabu cha IV cha Kuhusu Mafundisho ya Kikristo (On Christian Doctrine) alilipa kanisa mwongozo wake wa kwanza wa kuhubiri — muungano wa ajabu wa balagha ya kale na maudhui ya Kikristo, unaosisitiza kwamba mhubiri lazima alenge kufundisha, kufurahisha, na kusukuma wasikilizaji kutenda, kwa mpangilio huo. Kila kitabu cha kiada cha kuhubiri kilichofuata, pamoja na hiki, kimetokana na kitabu hicho.
9.4 The Sixteenth Century: The Reformers
9.4 Karne ya Kumi na Sita: Wanamatengenezo

Between the patristic pulpit and the Reformation pulpit lies a thousand years in which preaching never disappeared but largely lost its center. The medieval mass had become a watched event, not a heard one; the homily, when it occurred, was often a Latin reading nobody understood. The Reformers' great recovery was to put the preached Word back at the heart of Christian worship.

Kati ya mimbari ya Mababa wa Kanisa na mimbari ya Matengenezo kuna miaka elfu moja ambapo kuhubiri hakukutoweka kamwe, lakini kwa kiasi kikubwa kulipoteza kiini chake. Misa ya zama za kati ilikuwa imekuwa tukio la kutazamwa, si la kusikilizwa; homilia, ilipotolewa, mara nyingi ilikuwa somo la Kilatini ambalo hakuna aliyelielewa. Urejesho mkuu wa Wanamatengenezo ulikuwa kulirudisha Neno linalohubiriwa katika kiini cha ibada ya Kikristo.

Martin Luther (1483–1546) is the volcano. An Augustinian monk and professor at Wittenberg, he nailed his Ninety-Five Theses to the church door on October 31, 1517, and the Reformation began. He preached almost daily; an estimated two thousand of his sermons survive. But his greatest contribution to preaching was indirect: he translated the Bible into German so that the people in the pew could finally hear, in their own tongue, the text the preacher was preaching. He held that the preached Word — not the sacrament, not the liturgy, however valuable — is the foremost act of Christian worship, because it is the means by which faith comes (Romans 10:17). Where Luther's translation went, the preaching pulpit rose with it.

Martin Luther (1483–1546) ni volkano. Akiwa mtawa wa shirika la Augustino na profesa huko Wittenberg, aligongomea Hoja zake Tisini na Tano kwenye mlango wa kanisa tarehe 31 Oktoba 1517, na Matengenezo yakaanza. Alihubiri karibu kila siku; inakadiriwa kwamba mahubiri yake elfu mbili yamehifadhiwa. Lakini mchango wake mkubwa zaidi kwa kuhubiri haukuwa wa moja kwa moja: aliitafsiri Biblia kwa Kijerumani ili watu walioketi kanisani hatimaye waweze kusikia, kwa lugha yao wenyewe, kifungu ambacho mhubiri alikuwa akikihubiri. Alishikilia kwamba Neno linalohubiriwa — si sakramenti, si liturujia, hata kama vina thamani kiasi gani — ndilo tendo kuu la ibada ya Kikristo, kwa sababu ndilo njia ambayo imani huja (Warumi 10:17). Popote tafsiri ya Luther ilipokwenda, mimbari ya kuhubiri iliinuka pamoja nayo.

John Calvin (1509–1564) is the architect. Driven from France for his evangelical views, he settled reluctantly in Geneva and spent the rest of his life there teaching the city to think and preach biblically. He preached lectio continua — straight through entire books of the Bible — twice on Sundays and several weekdays. Roughly two thousand of his sermons were taken down by stenographers. His Institutes of the Christian Religion, written in his twenties and revised for the rest of his life, is the most influential systematic theology of the Reformation. Calvin shows the preacher that doctrinal depth and pulpit fire are not opposites — that the most rigorous theologian can also be the most pointed evangelist.

Yohana Calvin (1509–1564) ni mbunifu wa ujenzi. Akiwa amefukuzwa Ufaransa kwa sababu ya mitazamo yake ya kiinjili, alikaa Geneva bila kupenda sana, na akatumia maisha yake yote yaliyobaki huko akiufundisha mji kufikiri na kuhubiri kibiblia. Alihubiri lectio continua — moja kwa moja kupitia vitabu vizima vya Biblia — mara mbili kila Jumapili na siku kadhaa za katikati ya juma. Takriban mahubiri yake elfu mbili yaliandikwa na waandishi wa hati mkato. Kitabu chake Misingi ya Dini ya Kikristo (Institutes of the Christian Religion), alichokiandika akiwa na umri wa miaka ishirini na kitu na kukirekebisha maisha yake yote, ndiyo theolojia ya utaratibu yenye ushawishi mkubwa zaidi ya Matengenezo. Calvin anamwonyesha mhubiri kwamba kina cha mafundisho na moto wa mimbari si vitu vinavyopingana — kwamba mwanatheolojia aliye makini kuliko wote anaweza pia kuwa mwinjilisti mwenye ujumbe mkali na wa moja kwa moja kuliko wote.

Ulrich Zwingli (1484–1531) is the pioneer. Two years after Luther's theses, on January 1, 1519, Zwingli stood up at the Grossmünster in Zurich and announced that, instead of preaching the lectionary readings appointed for the church year, he would preach straight through the Gospel of Matthew, verse by verse, chapter by chapter, week by week. That was the day the Reformation pulpit was born as a recognizable thing. Calvin would perfect the method; Zwingli invented it. He died on the battlefield at Kappel in 1531, still in his forties, but the method he pioneered would outlive him by half a millennium and counting.

Ulrich Zwingli (1484–1531) ni mwanzilishi. Miaka miwili baada ya hoja za Luther, tarehe 1 Januari 1519, Zwingli alisimama katika kanisa la Grossmünster huko Zurich na kutangaza kwamba, badala ya kuhubiri masomo yaliyopangwa katika ratiba ya masomo ya mwaka wa kanisa (lekshenari), angehubiri moja kwa moja kupitia Injili ya Mathayo, mstari kwa mstari, sura kwa sura, juma kwa juma. Hiyo ndiyo siku ambayo mimbari ya Matengenezo ilizaliwa kama kitu kinachotambulika. Calvin angeikamilisha njia hiyo; Zwingli aliivumbua. Alikufa kwenye uwanja wa vita huko Kappel mwaka 1531, akiwa bado na umri wa miaka arobaini na kitu, lakini njia aliyoianzisha ingeishi baada yake kwa nusu ya milenia na zaidi.

John Knox (c. 1514–1572) is the prophet. The Scottish Reformer, trained in part by Calvin in Geneva, returned to a Scotland still bound to Rome and proceeded to dismantle the established church by preaching alone. His confrontations with Mary, Queen of Scots, are the stuff of legend — she said she feared his prayers more than an army of ten thousand men. His private prayer was famous: "Give me Scotland or I die." When the Reformation prevailed in Scotland in 1560, it was largely because John Knox would not stop preaching. His example to us is courage in the pulpit when the throne is in the pew.

Yohana Knox (takriban 1514–1572) ni nabii. Mwanamatengenezo huyu wa Uskoti, aliyefundishwa kwa sehemu na Calvin huko Geneva, alirudi Uskoti iliyokuwa bado imefungwa kwa Roma na akaendelea kulivunja kanisa rasmi la nchi kwa kuhubiri peke yake. Mapambano yake na Mary, Malkia wa Waskoti, ni mambo ya hekaya — malkia alisema aliogopa maombi yake kuliko jeshi la wanaume elfu kumi. Ombi lake la faragha lilikuwa maarufu: "Nipe Uskoti au nife." Matengenezo yaliposhinda Uskoti mwaka 1560, kwa kiasi kikubwa ilikuwa kwa sababu Yohana Knox hakukubali kuacha kuhubiri. Mfano wake kwetu ni ujasiri mimbarini wakati kiti cha enzi kiko kwenye benchi la kanisa.
9.5 The Nineteenth Century: The Great Pulpit Age
9.5 Karne ya Kumi na Tisa: Zama Kuu za Mimbari

The nineteenth century was a flowering. The Industrial Revolution had crowded the cities; the printing press could now ship sermons across continents within days; literacy had risen; and the awakening movements of the previous century had left whole nations open to gospel preaching. The result was a pulpit age unmatched before or since. Three figures will represent it.

Karne ya kumi na tisa ilikuwa wakati wa kuchanua. Mapinduzi ya Viwanda yalikuwa yamejaza miji watu; mashine ya uchapishaji sasa iliweza kusafirisha mahubiri kuvuka mabara ndani ya siku chache; kujua kusoma na kuandika kulikuwa kumeongezeka; na harakati za maamsho za karne iliyotangulia zilikuwa zimeacha mataifa mazima yakiwa wazi kwa mahubiri ya injili. Matokeo yake yalikuwa zama za mimbari zisizo na mfano kabla wala baada yake. Watu watatu watauwakilisha.

Charles Haddon Spurgeon (1834–1892) is the Prince of Preachers. Converted as a teenager during a snowstorm in a Primitive Methodist chapel, he was preaching by sixteen and pastoring his first church at seventeen. Called to New Park Street Chapel in London at nineteen, he soon outgrew it; the Metropolitan Tabernacle was built to seat six thousand and was full every Sunday for almost forty years. He preached without notes — only an outline on a small card — and he preached without a microphone in a building that seated six thousand people. His sermons were taken down by stenographers, printed each Wednesday morning, and shipped throughout the English-speaking world. He suffered chronic depression and chronic gout; he carried on preaching through both. He also founded a pastors' college, an orphanage, and over sixty other ministries. The published volumes of his sermons run to sixty-three thick books — the largest body of sermon literature ever produced by one preacher.

Charles Haddon Spurgeon (1834–1892) ni Mfalme wa Wahubiri. Aliongoka akiwa kijana wakati wa dhoruba ya theluji katika kanisa dogo la Wamethodisti wa Awali (Primitive Methodist), akawa anahubiri kufikia umri wa miaka kumi na sita na kuchunga kanisa lake la kwanza akiwa na miaka kumi na saba. Alipoitwa kwenye kanisa la New Park Street Chapel huko London akiwa na miaka kumi na tisa, punde lilimwia dogo; Metropolitan Tabernacle ilijengwa ili kuketisha watu elfu sita na ilijaa kila Jumapili kwa karibu miaka arobaini. Alihubiri bila maandishi — muhtasari tu kwenye kadi ndogo — na alihubiri bila kipaza sauti katika jengo lililoketisha watu elfu sita. Mahubiri yake yaliandikwa na waandishi wa hati mkato, yakachapishwa kila Jumatano asubuhi, na kusafirishwa katika ulimwengu wote unaozungumza Kiingereza. Aliteseka na sonona ya muda mrefu na ugonjwa wa gauti wa muda mrefu; aliendelea kuhubiri katika hali zote mbili. Pia alianzisha chuo cha wachungaji, kituo cha kulelea yatima, na huduma nyingine zaidi ya sitini. Juzuu zilizochapishwa za mahubiri yake zinafikia vitabu sitini na vitatu vinene — mkusanyiko mkubwa zaidi wa maandiko ya mahubiri uliowahi kutolewa na mhubiri mmoja.

Dwight L. Moody (1837–1899) is the lay evangelist. A Massachusetts farm boy who became a Chicago shoe salesman, he was converted at seventeen by a Sunday school teacher and never finished formal schooling. He never sought ordination and refused it when it was offered. He founded a Sunday school in the Chicago slums that grew into a church, then into an evangelistic empire that included two schools (Mount Hermon and Northfield) and the Bible institute in Chicago that now bears his name. He preached in the great hippodromes of London and the open fields of Iowa with equal effectiveness; he is said to have crossed the Atlantic more than a hundred times. The line most often quoted from him — "The world has yet to see what God will do with and for and through and in the man who is fully and wholly consecrated to him" — was reportedly spoken to him by Henry Varley; Moody is said to have responded, "By the grace of God, I'll be that man." Moody shows us that the seminary diploma is not the prerequisite for great preaching; the consecrated heart is.

Dwight L. Moody (1837–1899) ni mwinjilisti mlei. Akiwa mvulana wa shambani kutoka Massachusetts aliyekuja kuwa muuzaji wa viatu huko Chicago, aliongoka akiwa na miaka kumi na saba kupitia mwalimu wa Shule ya Jumapili na hakuwahi kumaliza masomo rasmi. Hakuwahi kutafuta kuwekwa wakfu kuwa mchungaji na alikataa alipopewa nafasi hiyo. Alianzisha Shule ya Jumapili katika mitaa ya maskini ya Chicago iliyokua ikawa kanisa, kisha ikawa huduma kubwa ya kiinjilisti iliyojumuisha shule mbili (Mount Hermon na Northfield) na chuo cha Biblia huko Chicago ambacho sasa kinaitwa kwa jina lake. Alihubiri katika viwanja vikubwa vya maonyesho (hipodromu) vya London na katika mashamba ya wazi ya Iowa kwa matokeo yale yale; inasemekana alivuka Bahari ya Atlantiki zaidi ya mara mia moja. Maneno yanayonukuliwa mara nyingi zaidi kutoka kwake — "Dunia bado haijaona kile Mungu atakachofanya pamoja na, kwa ajili ya, kupitia, na ndani ya mtu aliyejitoa wakfu kwake kikamilifu na kwa ukamilifu wote" — inasemekana kwamba yalisemwa kwake na Henry Varley; na Moody inasemekana alijibu, "Kwa neema ya Mungu, nitakuwa mtu huyo." Moody anatuonyesha kwamba cheti cha seminari si sharti la lazima la kuhubiri kwa ukuu; sharti ni moyo uliojitoa wakfu.

John Jasper (1812–1901) is the prophet of the African-American pulpit. Born a slave in Fluvanna County, Virginia, he was converted while working in a tobacco factory in Richmond and began preaching the same week. He could neither read nor write; he taught himself to read the Bible during stolen evening hours by spelling out one word at a time. After Emancipation he founded the Sixth Mt. Zion Baptist Church of Richmond in 1867; he pastored it the rest of his life. His most famous sermon, "De Sun Do Move" — a defense of the literal motion of the sun in answer to a parishioner unsettled by the new astronomy — he preached more than two hundred and fifty times across thirty-five years; people came from across the South to hear it, white as well as black. His life was written by William E. Hatcher, a white Baptist pastor in the same city, in a remarkable 1908 biography (John Jasper: The Unmatched Negro Philosopher and Preacher); a later treatment, Rhapsody in Black, brought his story to a wider audience. He stands as proof that the power of the pulpit has never been bound by literacy, race, or formal training, but by the Spirit of God resting on a soul yielded to Him.

Yohana Jasper (1812–1901) ni nabii wa mimbari ya Waamerika wenye asili ya Afrika. Alizaliwa mtumwa katika Kaunti ya Fluvanna, Virginia; aliongoka alipokuwa akifanya kazi katika kiwanda cha tumbaku huko Richmond na akaanza kuhubiri juma lile lile. Hakujua kusoma wala kuandika; alijifundisha mwenyewe kusoma Biblia katika saa za jioni alizoziiba, kwa kutamka herufi za neno moja baada ya jingine. Baada ya kukomeshwa kwa utumwa alianzisha kanisa la Sixth Mt. Zion Baptist Church la Richmond mwaka 1867; alilichunga maisha yake yote yaliyobaki. Mahubiri yake maarufu zaidi, "De Sun Do Move" ("Jua Linasonga") — utetezi wa mwendo halisi wa jua akimjibu mshiriki aliyekuwa amechanganyikiwa na elimu mpya ya nyota — aliyahubiri zaidi ya mara mia mbili na hamsini katika kipindi cha miaka thelathini na mitano; watu walikuja kutoka kila pembe ya Kusini kumsikia, wazungu kwa weusi. Wasifu wake uliandikwa na William E. Hatcher, mchungaji Mbaptisti mzungu katika mji ule ule, katika kitabu cha kipekee cha mwaka 1908 (John Jasper: The Unmatched Negro Philosopher and Preacher); maandiko ya baadaye, Rhapsody in Black, yaliifikisha habari yake kwa hadhira pana zaidi. Yeye anasimama kama ushahidi kwamba nguvu ya mimbari haijawahi kufungwa na kujua kusoma na kuandika, wala rangi ya ngozi, wala mafunzo rasmi, bali na Roho wa Mungu anayekaa juu ya nafsi iliyojitoa kwake.
9.6 Honorable Mentions
9.6 Wanaostahili Kutajwa Pia

Other centuries had their giants too. Girolamo Savonarola (1452–1498) preached against the corruptions of Renaissance Florence with such fire that the city was at one point ruled from his pulpit; he was hanged and burned in 1498 — a forerunner of the Reformation by twenty years. John Wesley (1703–1791) and George Whitefield (1714–1770), in the eighteenth century, took the gospel out of the parish church and into the open fields of England and the American colonies; Whitefield's open-air crowds sometimes numbered twenty to thirty thousand without amplification. Charles Finney (1792–1875), a New York lawyer turned evangelist, was the transitional figure between the awakenings and the modern revivalism; his "new measures" provoked both revival and controversy. And in our own twentieth century, Billy Graham (1918–2018) carried the simple gospel of John 3:16 to more people, in person, than any preacher in history — an estimated two hundred fifteen million on six continents. They are not in the four great centuries because their centuries belong, on balance, elsewhere; but each is a gift to the universal church.

Karne nyingine pia zilikuwa na majitu yao. Girolamo Savonarola (1452–1498) alihubiri dhidi ya maovu ya Florence ya zama za Mwamko (Renaissance) kwa moto mkubwa kiasi kwamba wakati fulani mji ulitawaliwa kutoka mimbari yake; alinyongwa na kuchomwa moto mwaka 1498 — mtangulizi wa Matengenezo kwa miaka ishirini. Yohana Wesley (1703–1791) na George Whitefield (1714–1770), katika karne ya kumi na nane, waliitoa injili nje ya kanisa la parokia na kuipeleka kwenye mashamba ya wazi ya Uingereza na makoloni ya Amerika; makutano ya Whitefield ya nje wakati mwingine yalifikia watu elfu ishirini hadi thelathini bila vipaza sauti. Charles Finney (1792–1875), mwanasheria wa New York aliyegeuka kuwa mwinjilisti, alikuwa kiungo kati ya maamsho na harakati za kisasa za mikutano ya uamsho; "mbinu zake mpya" zilizaa uamsho na pia ubishi. Na katika karne yetu ya ishirini, Billy Graham (1918–2018) aliipeleka injili rahisi ya Yohana 3:16 kwa watu wengi zaidi, ana kwa ana, kuliko mhubiri yeyote katika historia — inakadiriwa watu milioni mia mbili na kumi na tano katika mabara sita. Hawamo katika zile karne nne kuu kwa sababu karne zao, kwa jumla, zinahusika mahali pengine; lakini kila mmoja wao ni zawadi kwa kanisa la ulimwengu wote.
9.7 What All Four Eras Share
9.7 Kile Ambacho Nyakati Zote Nne Zinashiriki

Look across the four centuries and a common DNA appears. First, every great preaching era was a Word era. Peter preached the Psalms and the Prophets; Chrysostom preached straight through Romans and Matthew; the Reformers' watchword was sola Scriptura; Spurgeon's outlines were verses, not topics. Where the text is honored, the pulpit is renewed; where the text is replaced with something cleverer, the pulpit dies. Second, every great preaching era was a courage era. Stephen was stoned, Chrysostom exiled, Luther outlawed, Knox imprisoned, Jasper born into slavery — and each kept preaching. The pulpit costs something. Third, every great preaching era preached Christ. Paul on Mars Hill, Augustine in Hippo, Luther in Wittenberg, Spurgeon in London, Jasper in Richmond — the name on their lips was the same name. The preacher's job has never changed: to lift Jesus up before a world that, when it sees Him, comes (John 12:32). Fourth, every great preaching era was a Spirit era. Pentecost without the Spirit would have been Peter giving a speech. Chrysostom without the Spirit would have been a clever rhetorician. Luther without the Spirit would have been an academic. The seven skills you have learned in this course are the bow; the Spirit of God is the arrow. Never pretend that one without the other will hit the mark.

Tazama katika karne zote nne na utaona vinasaba (DNA) vya pamoja vikijitokeza. Kwanza, kila wakati mkuu wa kuhubiri ulikuwa wakati wa Neno. Petro alihubiri Zaburi na Manabii; Krisostomo alihubiri moja kwa moja kupitia Warumi na Mathayo; kauli mbiu ya Wanamatengenezo ilikuwa sola Scriptura (Maandiko peke yake); mihtasari ya Spurgeon ilikuwa mistari ya Biblia, si mada. Pale kifungu kinapoheshimiwa, mimbari hufanywa upya; pale kifungu kinapobadilishwa na kitu kinachoonekana cha werevu zaidi, mimbari hufa. Pili, kila wakati mkuu wa kuhubiri ulikuwa wakati wa ujasiri. Stefano alipigwa mawe, Krisostomo alifukuzwa uhamishoni, Luther alitangazwa kuwa mhalifu, Knox alifungwa, Jasper alizaliwa katika utumwa — na kila mmoja aliendelea kuhubiri. Mimbari hugharimu kitu. Tatu, kila wakati mkuu wa kuhubiri ulimhubiri Kristo. Paulo juu ya Areopago, Augustino huko Hippo, Luther huko Wittenberg, Spurgeon huko London, Jasper huko Richmond — jina lililokuwa midomoni mwao lilikuwa jina lile lile. Kazi ya mhubiri haijawahi kubadilika: kumwinua Yesu mbele ya ulimwengu ambao, unapomwona, huja kwake (Yohana 12:32). Nne, kila wakati mkuu wa kuhubiri ulikuwa wakati wa Roho. Pentekoste bila Roho ingekuwa Petro akitoa hotuba tu. Krisostomo bila Roho angekuwa mtaalamu wa balagha mwerevu tu. Luther bila Roho angekuwa msomi tu. Ujuzi saba ulioujifunza katika kozi hii ni upinde; Roho wa Mungu ni mshale. Usijidanganye kamwe kwamba kimoja bila kingine kitapiga shabaha.

You are about to finish this course. When you do, the same Spirit who anointed every preacher on this list is the Spirit who has been given to you (Acts 1:8). The four great centuries are not closed. There is no reason a fifth great century could not begin in your generation, in your pulpit, in your town. The men in this unit had no advantage over you that matters — they had paper and ink, you have keyboards and platforms; they had crowds, you have congregations; they had the same Holy Spirit. Go and preach.

Uko karibu kumaliza kozi hii. Utakapoimaliza, Roho yule yule aliyempaka mafuta kila mhubiri katika orodha hii ndiye Roho uliyepewa wewe (Matendo 1:8). Zile karne nne kuu hazijafungwa. Hakuna sababu kwa nini karne kuu ya tano isianze katika kizazi chako, katika mimbari yako, katika mji wako. Wanaume walio katika sehemu hii hawakuwa na faida yoyote juu yako yenye maana — wao walikuwa na karatasi na wino, wewe una kibodi na majukwaa; wao walikuwa na makutano, wewe una makusanyiko; wao walikuwa na Roho Mtakatifu yule yule. Nenda ukahubiri.
